example2_en: Shops in front of a school affect what students buy more than a poster inside the classroom does.
example2_zh: 学校前面的商店对学生买什么的影响，大于教室里的一张海报。
collocations: in front of｜在……前面 ; in the front of｜在……前部
tip_zh: in front of 在外部前面；in the front of 在内部的前部。

meanings_zh: adj. 熟悉的 | adj. 熟知的；了解的
definition_en: well known | having knowledge or experience of something
example1_en: This song sounds familiar.
example1_zh: 这首歌听起来很熟悉。
example2_en: Students who are familiar with digital tools may adapt more easily to online learning environments.
example2_zh: 熟悉数字工具的学生可能更容易适应在线学习环境。
collocations: familiar with｜熟悉…… ; familiar to｜为……所熟悉 ; a familiar face｜熟悉的面孔 ; look familiar｜看起来眼熟
tip_zh: 人熟悉事物用with；事物为人熟悉用to。

definition_en: the dark part of the day
example1_en: I review new words at night.
example1_zh: 我在晚上复习生词。
example2_en: Bright signs at night may help shops, but they can also keep nearby residents awake.
example2_zh: 夜间明亮的招牌也许有助于商店，但也会让附近居民睡不着。
collocations: at night｜在夜里 ; last night｜昨晚 ; night and day｜日夜
tip_zh: at night 不加 the；on 加具体的某个夜晚，如 on Sunday night。

definition_en: to put a question, or to request
example1_en: Ask the teacher if you do not understand.
example1_zh: 不懂就问老师。
example2_en: Cities should ask residents where floods actually reach, not only where the map predicts them.
example2_zh: 城市应该询问居民洪水实际淹到哪里，而不只是看地图的预测。
collocations: ask for｜请求 ; ask sb to do｜请某人做
tip_zh: ask sb sth 或 ask sb to do。ask 后不接 sb doing。

meanings_zh: n. 火；火灾 | v. 开火；解雇
definition_en: burning, or a destructive burning | to shoot, or to dismiss from a job
example1_en: We had a fire drill on Monday.
example1_zh: 周一我们进行了消防演习。
example2_en: A hillside fire can reach a village faster than a warning if the road out is narrow.
example2_zh: 如果出去的路很窄，山火到达村庄的速度可以快过警报。
collocations: on fire｜着火 ; fire alarm｜火警 ; set fire to｜点燃
tip_zh: fire 作“火”时常不可数；一场火灾用 a fire。

definition_en: to be worthy of
example1_en: You deserve a rest after such hard work.
example1_zh: 这么辛苦之后你应得休息。
example2_en: Healthcare workers deserve greater recognition because their dedication contributes directly to the wellbeing of society.
example2_zh: 医护人员值得获得更多认可，因为他们的奉献直接促进了社会福祉。
collocations: deserve praise｜值得表扬 ; deserve attention｜值得关注 ; deserve to win｜理应获胜
tip_zh: 接名词或to do；不用deserve doing表示主动。

meanings_zh: adj. 精神的；心理的 | adj. 脑力的；在头脑中进行的
definition_en: of the mind | Using thought rather than physical action or written calculation.
example1_en: mental health matters as much as body health.
example1_zh: 心理健康与身体健康同样重要。
example2_en: Employers should give mental wellbeing the same priority as physical safety when designing workplace policies.
example2_zh: 雇主制定职场政策时，应将心理健康与人身安全放在同等重要的位置。
collocations: mental health｜心理健康 ; mental wellbeing｜心理幸福感 ; mental arithmetic｜心算 ; mental effort｜脑力付出
tip_zh: mental侧重心理或脑力；口语中形容人疯狂可能冒犯。

definition_en: the reflexive form of you
example1_en: Please help yourself to the fruit.
example1_zh: 请随便吃水果。
example2_en: You should ask yourself who benefits before you share a story that sounds too perfect.
example2_zh: 在转发一个听起来过于完美的故事之前，你应该问问自己谁从中获益。
collocations: by yourself｜独自 ; help yourself｜请自便
tip_zh: 对多人用 yourselves。

meanings_zh: v. 有益于 | v. 使受益；得益于 | n. 福利金；补助金
definition_en: to be good for | to help someone or receive help or an advantage | money provided by the government to people needing support
example1_en: Exercise can benefit both body and mind.
example1_zh: 锻炼有益于身心。
example2_en: Rural communities can benefit from improved internet access through greater opportunities for education and employment.
example2_zh: 更好的互联网接入能增加教育和就业机会，让农村社区受益。
collocations: health benefits｜健康益处 ; benefit from｜从……中受益 ; unemployment benefit｜失业救济金 ; mutual benefit｜互利
tip_zh: benefit sb指使某人受益；benefit from指得益于。

definition_en: a being believed to control nature or life
example1_en: In the story, the villagers thanked the god of the river.
example1_zh: 故事里，村民感谢河神。
example2_en: Ancient myths about a god of rain show how closely people once tied weather to survival.
example2_zh: 古代关于雨神的神话表明，人们曾经把天气和生存联系得多么紧密。
collocations: thank God｜谢天谢地
tip_zh: god 指神灵；God 大写时常特指基督教等宗教中的上帝。

definition_en: a place where legal cases are heard, or a sports ground
example1_en: The tennis court is behind the gym.
example1_zh: 网球场在体育馆后面。
example2_en: A court that takes years to hear a simple case leaves families waiting for a decision.
example2_zh: 审理一件简单案件要花数年的法院，会让家庭一直等一个决定。
collocations: basketball court｜篮球场 ; go to court｜上法庭
tip_zh: court 既可指法庭也可指球场，要看搭配。

definition_en: done for only part of the usual working time
example1_en: She has a part-time job at the library.
example1_zh: 她在图书馆有一份兼职。
example2_en: Part-time jobs can teach responsibility, but they should not replace the sleep teenagers still need.
example2_zh: 兼职可以培养责任感，但不该取代青少年仍然需要的睡眠。
collocations: part-time job｜兼职工作 ; full-time｜全职的
tip_zh: part-time 作定语时通常加连字符；作状语有时写成 part time。

meanings_zh: adj. 最后的；最近的 | v. 持续
definition_en: coming after all others, or most recent | to continue for a period of time
example1_en: I sat in the last row during the talk.
example1_zh: 讲座时我坐在最后一排。
example2_en: Last year's flood still shapes where the town is willing to build new houses.
example2_zh: 去年的洪水仍然影响着这座城镇愿意在哪里建新房。
collocations: at last｜终于 ; last night｜昨晚 ; the last but not least｜最后但同样重要
tip_zh: last 作动词是“持续”。过去式和过去分词仍是 last。

meanings_zh: n. 背景 | n. 背景情况 | n. 背景；后景
definition_en: past experience or setting | Information or events needed to understand a situation | The part of a scene behind the main subject
example1_en: Her family background shaped her views.
example1_zh: 她的家庭背景塑造了她的观点。
example2_en: Universities should provide equal opportunities for applicants from different social backgrounds, regardless of their family income.
example2_zh: 大学应为来自不同社会背景的申请者提供平等机会，不论其家庭收入如何。
collocations: a professional background｜职业背景 ; background information｜背景资料 ; in the background｜在背景中 ; a disadvantaged background｜弱势家庭背景
tip_zh: 经历领域用background in；背景中用in the background。

meanings_zh: adj. 直接的 | v. 指导；指挥；导演 | v. 指路；将……指向
definition_en: straight; clear | To guide or control an activity, performance, or group. | To show the way or aim something towards a place.
example1_en: Take the direct route home.
example1_zh: 走直接回家的路。
example2_en: Improved public transport can have a direct impact on employment by connecting residents with more job opportunities.
example2_zh: 改善公共交通能让居民获得更多就业机会，从而对就业产生直接影响。
collocations: direct contact｜直接接触 ; a direct flight｜直达航班 ; direct a film｜导演电影 ; direct attention to｜将注意力转向
tip_zh: direct可作形容词或动词；常见读音也有/daɪˈrekt/。

definition_en: fighting between countries or groups
example1_en: The history class discussed the cost of war.
example1_zh: 历史课讨论了战争的代价。
example2_en: After a war, schools are often rebuilt later than roads, though children need them first.
example2_zh: 战争之后，学校的重建常常晚于道路，尽管孩子最先需要的是学校。
collocations: world war｜世界大战 ; at war｜处于战争中
tip_zh: war 前常用 in：in the war。

definition_en: teaching and learning
example1_en: Public education should not depend on a family's income.
example1_zh: 公共教育不该取决于一个家庭的收入。
example2_en: Education about floods is useful only when it includes the streets children actually use.
example2_zh: 关于洪水的教育，只有包含孩子真正走的那些街时才有用。
collocations: higher education｜高等教育 ; physical education｜体育
tip_zh: education 不可数。

definition_en: a female child
example1_en: The girl by the window is our monitor.
example1_zh: 窗边的女孩是我们的班长。
example2_en: A girl who wants to study engineering should see women doing that work, not only hear that it is possible.
example2_zh: 想学工程的女孩，应该看到有女性在做这份工作，而不只是听说这是可能的。
collocations: little girl｜小女孩
tip_zh: girl 的复数是 girls。

definition_en: a row, a long mark, or a queue
example1_en: Please stand in line for the tickets.
example1_zh: 请排队买票。
example2_en: A new metro line helps the centre, but outer towns still need buses to reach the first station.
example2_zh: 新地铁线方便市中心，但外围城镇仍需要公交才能到第一站。
collocations: in line｜排队 ; on line｜在线上 ; wait in line｜排队等候
tip_zh: 排队英式常用 queue，美式常用 line。online 是一个词，表示“在线”。

meanings_zh: v. 找到（find 的过去式） | v. 建立
definition_en: past tense of find | to start an organisation
example1_en: We found a quiet corner in the library.
example1_zh: 我们在图书馆找到一个安静的角落。
example2_en: Archaeologists found tools that show people cooked together long before cities existed.
example2_zh: 考古学家发现的工具表明，早在城市出现之前，人们就一起做饭了。
collocations: found out｜查明（过去式）
tip_zh: find 的过去式是 found。表示“建立”时 founded 才是过去式，不要混用。

definition_en: a part of a building, or space for something
example1_en: The music room is on the second floor.
example1_zh: 音乐教室在二楼。
example2_en: There is little room for a safe pavement if cars are allowed to park on both sides.
example2_zh: 如果允许汽车停在两边，就几乎没有空间做安全的人行道。
collocations: make room for｜为……腾地方 ; reading room｜阅览室
tip_zh: room 表示空间时不可数：no room for。表示房间时可数。

meanings_zh: v. 使困惑 | v. 混淆；认错
definition_en: to make unclear or mixed up | To wrongly think one person or thing is another.
example1_en: Too many choices may confuse buyers.
example1_zh: 选择太多可能让买家困惑。
example2_en: Public health messages can confuse audiences when experts use technical language without explaining its meaning.
example2_zh: 专家使用术语却不解释其含义时，公共卫生信息可能会让受众感到困惑。
collocations: confuse A with B｜把A与B混淆 ; confuse the issue｜把问题弄复杂 ; easily confused｜容易混淆的
tip_zh: confused形容人感到困惑；confusing形容事物令人困惑。

definition_en: a person
example1_en: Every human being needs clean water.
example1_zh: 每个人都需要干净的水。
example2_en: A human being waiting for a bus in the dark is not a traffic statistic; the street should be lit.
example2_zh: 在黑暗中等公交的人不是一个交通统计数字；街道应该有灯。
collocations: human beings｜人们
tip_zh: human being 比 human 更强调“人”这一完整说法，可数。

meanings_zh: v. 观看；注视 | n. 手表
definition_en: to look at something for a time | a small clock worn on the wrist
example1_en: We watched the match in the hall.
example1_zh: 我们在大厅看了比赛。
example2_en: Residents watch a river rise long before an official warning reaches their phones.
example2_zh: 居民在官方警报到达手机之前很久，就看着河水上涨。
collocations: watch out｜当心 ; watch TV｜看电视
tip_zh: watch 强调持续看；see 强调看见的结果。

meanings_zh: adj. 好奇的 | adj. 奇怪的；不寻常的
definition_en: wanting to know more | Unusual or strange in a way that attracts attention.
example1_en: Children are curious about nature.
example1_zh: 孩子对自然充满好奇。
example2_en: Teachers can encourage curious students to explore scientific questions through practical experiments rather than memorisation alone.
example2_zh: 教师可以鼓励求知欲强的学生通过动手实验探索科学问题，而不只是死记硬背。
collocations: curious about｜对……好奇 ; curious to know｜很想知道 ; a curious mixture｜奇特的混合物
tip_zh: be curious about表示“对……好奇”。

definition_en: on some occasions but not always
example1_en: I sometimes study in the library.
example1_zh: 我有时在图书馆学习。
example2_en: Buses that sometimes skip a stop leave students guessing whether to wait or walk.
example2_zh: 有时甩站的公交，让学生猜测该等还是该走。
collocations: sometimes...sometimes｜有时……有时
tip_zh: sometimes 位置较灵活，可放句首、句中或句末。

meanings_zh: v. 控制；管理 | n. 控制
definition_en: to have power over something | the power to decide
example1_en: We cannot control the weather, but we can plan for rain.
example1_zh: 我们控制不了天气，但可以为下雨做准备。
example2_en: Cities that control building near rivers reduce the damage when the water rises.
example2_zh: 控制河边建设的城市，能在水位上涨时减少损失。
collocations: under control｜处于控制中 ; out of control｜失控 ; control over｜对……的控制
tip_zh: control 的过去式仍是 control，过去分词加 -led：controlled。

meanings_zh: v. 开始；出发 | n. 开始
definition_en: to begin | the beginning of something
example1_en: We start the meeting at two.
example1_zh: 我们两点开始开会。
example2_en: Cities that start rubbish sorting early avoid the higher cost of fixing mixed waste later.
example2_zh: 早点开始垃圾分类的城市，可以避免以后处理混合垃圾的更高成本。
collocations: start doing｜开始做 ; start with｜从……开始 ; from the start｜从一开始
tip_zh: start 和 begin 后接 to do 或 doing 通常都可以。

definition_en: the state of being alive, or a way of living
example1_en: School life is busy but full of friends.
example1_zh: 学校生活忙碌，但有很多朋友。
example2_en: City life can be exciting, yet the noise and cost push some families back to smaller towns.
example2_zh: 城市生活可以很精彩，但噪音和花费也会把一些家庭推回小城镇。
collocations: way of life｜生活方式 ; all one's life｜一生 ; daily life｜日常生活
tip_zh: life 的复数是 lives。泛指生活时通常不可数。

definition_en: a large town
example1_en: Our city has a new metro line.
example1_zh: 我们这座城市有一条新地铁线。
example2_en: A city that grows upward needs parks on the ground, or children will have nowhere to play.
example2_zh: 向上生长的城市需要地面上的公园，否则孩子将无处玩耍。
collocations: capital city｜首都 ; city centre｜市中心
tip_zh: city 的复数是 cities。in the city 表示在城里。

meanings_zh: n. 研究 | v. 研究
definition_en: careful study to find facts | to study something carefully
example1_en: Her research is about teenage sleep.
example1_zh: 她的研究是关于青少年睡眠的。
example2_en: Research that never leaves the lab may miss what families actually do at home.
example2_zh: 从不离开实验室的研究，可能会错过家庭在家里真正做的事。
collocations: do research｜做研究 ; research into｜对……的研究
tip_zh: research 作研究时通常不可数。作动词直接接宾语：research a topic。

definition_en: in the middle of three or more
example1_en: She is the tallest among the three.
example1_zh: 她是三人中最高的。
example2_en: Trust is low among residents when a new road is planned without a public meeting.
example2_zh: 如果新路的规划没有公开会议，居民之间的信任就会很低。
collocations: among other things｜除了别的以外
tip_zh: among 用于三者或更多；between 多用于两者。

definition_en: land for crops, an area of study, or a sports ground
example1_en: The football field is behind the gym.
example1_zh: 足球场在体育馆后面。
example2_en: Experts in one field may miss a river problem that farmers in the next field see every week.
example2_zh: 一个领域的专家可能会错过隔壁田里的农民每周都看见的河流问题。
collocations: in the field of｜在……领域 ; field trip｜实地考察
tip_zh: field 既可指田野、运动场，也可指学术领域。

meanings_zh: adv. 今天 | n. 今天
definition_en: on this day | this day
example1_en: Today we will practise the listening section.
example1_zh: 今天我们练习听力部分。
example2_en: Decisions made today about housing will decide who can live near good schools in ten years.
example2_zh: 今天做出的住房决定，将决定十年后谁能住在好学校附近。
collocations: today's newspaper｜今天的报纸
tip_zh: today 可作副词或名词，前面不加介词 on。

meanings_zh: prep. 自……以来 | conj. 自从；因为
definition_en: from a time in the past until now | from the time when, or because
example1_en: I have lived here since 2019.
example1_zh: 我从 2019 年起住在这里。
example2_en: Since the new bridge opened, fewer students have had to take two buses to reach school.
example2_zh: 自从新桥通车，需要换乘两趟公交才能到校的学生少了。
collocations: ever since｜从那时起一直 ; since then｜从那时起
tip_zh: since 接时间点，for 接时间段，常与现在完成时连用。

definition_en: paid work, or a task
example1_en: She found a weekend job at a bookshop.
example1_zh: 她在书店找到一份周末工作。
example2_en: A first job teaches timekeeping, but it should not take the hours a student needs for sleep.
example2_zh: 第一份工作能培养守时，但不该占掉学生需要的睡眠时间。
collocations: job interview｜求职面试 ; out of a job｜失业 ; do a good job｜干得好
tip_zh: job 是可数名词，一份工作用 a job；work 表示工作通常不可数。

meanings_zh: adj. 杰出的；明亮的 | adj. 才华出众的；聪颖的 | adj. 明亮的；灿烂的
definition_en: very clever or bright | Exceptionally intelligent or skilled. | Shining brightly or having a strong, vivid colour.
example1_en: She had a brilliant idea.
example1_zh: 她有一个杰出的想法。
example2_en: Brilliant teachers can inspire students to explore difficult subjects with confidence and genuine curiosity.
example2_zh: 出色的教师能激励学生带着信心和真正的好奇心探索难学的科目。
collocations: brilliant idea｜绝妙的主意 ; brilliant scientist｜杰出的科学家 ; brilliant sunshine｜灿烂的阳光
tip_zh: 英式口语中常用 brilliant 表示“太棒了”。

definition_en: happening every day
example1_en: Exercise is part of her daily routine.
example1_zh: 锻炼是她每日例行的一部分。

meanings_zh: n. 北；北方 | adj. 北方的
definition_en: the direction opposite south | in or towards the north
example1_en: The wind is coming from the north.
example1_zh: 风从北边来。
example2_en: Towns in the north may need longer heating seasons, which raises the cost of keeping schools warm.
example2_zh: 北方城镇可能需要更长的供暖季，这会提高学校保暖的成本。
collocations: in the north｜在北方 ; north of｜在……以北
tip_zh: in the north of 在范围内部的北部；to the north of 在某地以北。

definition_en: expected, or owed
example1_en: The report is due on Friday.
example1_zh: 报告周五到期。
example2_en: Floods are due in part to drains built for a smaller town than the one that exists now.
example2_zh: 洪水的部分原因是排水系统按比现在更小的城镇修建。
collocations: due to｜由于 ; be due to do｜预定做
tip_zh: due to 后接名词，表示原因；be due to do 表示预定要做。

definition_en: a set of parts working together, or an organised method
example1_en: The school bell system was repaired yesterday.
example1_zh: 学校的铃声系统昨天修好了。
example2_en: A bus system that only serves the centre leaves outer neighbourhoods with long walks to the first stop.
example2_zh: 只服务市中心的公交系统，会让外围社区走到第一站就要很久。
collocations: public system｜公共系统 ; system of｜……的体系
tip_zh: system 是可数名词：a transport system。

definition_en: to go away, or to let something stay
example1_en: We leave school at four on Fridays.
example1_zh: 周五我们四点离校。
example2_en: If young people leave a town, the shops and clinics that depend on them leave too.
example2_zh: 如果年轻人离开城镇，依靠他们的商店和诊所也会离开。
collocations: leave for｜动身去 ; leave out｜遗漏 ; leave a message｜留口信
tip_zh: leave 的过去式和过去分词是 left。leave 也可表示“使处于某种状态”：leave the door open。

definition_en: to say sorry
example1_en: You should apologize for being late.
example1_zh: 你应该为迟到道歉。
example2_en: Companies should apologize promptly for service failures and explain what steps they will take to prevent further problems.
example2_zh: 企业应及时为服务失误道歉，并说明将采取哪些措施来防止问题再次发生。
collocations: apologize to someone｜向某人道歉 ; apologize for doing something｜为做某事道歉 ; apologize sincerely｜真诚道歉
tip_zh: 向人道歉用to，为事情道歉用for；英式也写apologise。

meanings_zh: v. 试图；尝试 | n. 尝试
definition_en: to make an effort, or to test something | an attempt
example1_en: Try the second method if the first one fails.
example1_zh: 如果第一种方法不行，试试第二种。
example2_en: Cities should try small bus changes before they rebuild a whole road.
example2_zh: 城市在重建整条路之前，应该先尝试小的公交调整。
collocations: try to do｜努力做 ; try doing｜试着做 ; have a try｜试一试
tip_zh: try to do 强调努力要做成；try doing 强调试一试某种做法。

definition_en: a male parent
example1_en: My father picks me up on Fridays.
example1_zh: 我父亲周五来接我。
example2_en: A father who works nights may never see the school play his child is in.
example2_zh: 上夜班的父亲可能永远看不到孩子参加的学校演出。
collocations: father and mother｜父母
tip_zh: father 是较正式的说法；dad 更口语。

definition_en: something that is done
example1_en: We need action, not only a poster.
example1_zh: 我们需要行动，而不只是一张海报。
example2_en: Climate action in a city includes buses and buildings, not only speeches on a special day.
example2_zh: 一座城市的气候行动包括公交和建筑，而不只是特殊日子里的演讲。
collocations: take action｜采取行动 ; in action｜在运转
tip_zh: take action to do 表示采取行动做某事。

meanings_zh: num. 第二；秒 | n. 秒；片刻
definition_en: the one after the first, or a unit of time | a very short time
example1_en: I sat in the second row.
example1_zh: 我坐在第二排。
example2_en: A delay of even a second at a busy junction can add up to long queues in the evening.
example2_zh: 繁忙路口哪怕一秒钟的延误，也会在傍晚累积成长队。
collocations: a second｜再一个 ; second-hand｜二手的
tip_zh: the second 表示顺序；a second 可以表示“又一”。

definition_en: not high
example1_en: The shelf is low enough for everyone to reach.
example1_zh: 架子低得每个人都够得着。
example2_en: Low pay in village schools makes it hard to keep teachers who could work in the city.
example2_zh: 乡村学校的低报酬，让那些可以去城市工作的老师很难留下来。
collocations: low price｜低价 ; at a low level｜处于低水平
tip_zh: low 的比较级是 lower。人的声音低用 a low voice。

meanings_zh: v. 移动；搬家；感动 | n. 行动；一步
definition_en: to change place, or to cause a feeling | an action
example1_en: Please move your bag off the seat.
example1_zh: 请把包从座位上移开。
example2_en: Families move away when rents rise faster than wages, and schools then lose students.
example2_zh: 当房租涨得比工资快时，家庭会搬走，学校随后失去学生。
collocations: move to｜搬到 ; move on｜继续前进 ; be moved｜被感动
tip_zh: move 可作及物或不及物。搬家用 move to a place。

definition_en: a series of names or items
example1_en: Your name is not on the list.
example1_zh: 名单上没有你的名字。
example2_en: A waiting list for a clinic shows demand, but it does not treat the patient.
example2_zh: 诊所的等候名单显示需求，但并不治疗病人。
collocations: a list of｜一份……清单 ; make a list｜列清单
tip_zh: list 作动词是“列出”。

definition_en: to come together, or to satisfy a need
example1_en: We will meet at the gate at seven.
example1_zh: 我们七点在门口见面。
example2_en: A bus timetable should meet the hour when school ends, not an office hour from another city.
example2_zh: 公交时刻应该配合放学的时间，而不是另一座城市的办公时间。
collocations: meet with｜会见 ; sports meet｜运动会
tip_zh: meet 的过去式和过去分词是 met。初次相识用 meet；重逢也用 meet。

definition_en: to remain in a place or state
example1_en: Please stay in your seat until the bell.
example1_zh: 铃响前请留在座位上。
example2_en: Young workers stay in a town only if housing and jobs appear together.
example2_zh: 只有住房和工作同时出现，年轻工人才会留在城镇。
collocations: stay up｜熬夜 ; stay away｜离开 ; stay healthy｜保持健康
tip_zh: stay 作连系动词后接形容词：stay calm。

definition_en: feeling pleasure
example1_en: I am happy to help with the posters.
example1_zh: 我乐意帮忙做海报。
example2_en: A happy photo of a new park hides the families who were moved to make space for it.
example2_zh: 新公园的快乐照片，藏起了为腾地方而被搬走的家庭。
collocations: be happy to do｜乐意做 ; happy with｜对……满意
tip_zh: happy 后接 to do 或 that 从句。

meanings_zh: adj. 自信的 | adj. 确信的；有把握的
definition_en: sure of yourself | certain that something is true or will happen
example1_en: Speak in a confident voice.
example1_zh: 用自信的声音说话。
example2_en: Students become more confident when teachers provide constructive feedback and opportunities to practise new skills.
example2_zh: 当教师提供建设性反馈和练习新技能的机会时，学生会变得更自信。
collocations: feel confident｜感到自信 ; confident about the future｜对未来有信心 ; confident that｜确信
tip_zh: confident是形容词；confidence是名词。

definition_en: things that people or animals eat
example1_en: The food in the canteen was simple but hot.
example1_zh: 食堂的食物简单但是热的。
example2_en: Wasted food in school kitchens is a loss of money and of the water used to grow it.
example2_zh: 学校厨房里浪费的食物，既是金钱的损失，也是种植它所用水的损失。
collocations: fast food｜快餐 ; food and drink｜饮食
tip_zh: food 通常不可数。一种食物可以说 a food，但较少用。

definition_en: sounds arranged in a way people enjoy
example1_en: There is music practice in the hall after school.
example1_zh: 放学后大厅里有音乐排练。
example2_en: Live music in a square can bring a neighbourhood together, but only if the volume lets people talk.
example2_zh: 广场上的现场音乐能把社区聚在一起，但前提是音量仍允许人们交谈。
collocations: pop music｜流行音乐 ; music lesson｜音乐课
tip_zh: music 不可数，不说 a music 或 musics。

meanings_zh: n. 问题 | v. 质疑
definition_en: something you ask | to express doubt about
example1_en: May I ask a question about the homework?
example1_zh: 我可以问一个关于作业的问题吗？
example2_en: The right question about a new road is who will walk it, not only how many cars it will carry.
example2_zh: 关于一条新路，正确的问题是谁会在上面走，而不只是它能载多少车。
collocations: ask a question｜提问 ; out of the question｜不可能 ; in question｜讨论中的
tip_zh: out of the question 是“不可能”；out of question 现在很少用。

definition_en: despite the fact that
example1_en: Though the lab is small, the equipment is new.
example1_zh: 虽然实验室小，设备却是新的。
example2_en: Though a city plants trees, the streets stay hot if the trees are too young to give shade.
example2_zh: 尽管一座城市种了树，如果树还小、遮不成荫，街道依然炎热。
collocations: even though｜即使 ; as though｜好像
tip_zh: though 可放在句首或句末；although 多放在句首，一般不放句末。

definition_en: if, used when there are two possibilities
example1_en: I do not know whether the museum is open.
example1_zh: 我不知道博物馆是否开着。
example2_en: Whether a town keeps its clinic depends on buses as well as on doctors.
example2_zh: 一个城镇能否保住诊所，既取决于医生，也取决于公交。
collocations: whether...or｜是……还是 ; whether or not｜是否
tip_zh: whether 可接不定式：whether to go。if 一般不接不定式。介词后用 whether，不用 if。

definition_en: new information about events
example1_en: The news about the match spread quickly.
example1_zh: 关于比赛的消息很快传开了。
example2_en: Good news reporting explains what is known and what is still uncertain.
example2_zh: 好的新闻报道会说明哪些是已知的，哪些仍不确定。
collocations: a piece of news｜一则新闻 ; news report｜新闻报道
tip_zh: news 不可数，不说 a news。一则新闻用 a piece of news。

definition_en: a unit of language
example1_en: I wrote the new word in my notebook.
example1_zh: 我把生词写在笔记本里。
example2_en: A single word in a headline can change how readers judge a whole event.
example2_zh: 标题里的一个词就能改变读者对整件事的判断。
collocations: in other words｜换句话说 ; keep one's word｜守信 ; word for word｜逐字
tip_zh: have a word with sb 是和某人说句话；have words with 是争吵。

definition_en: probable
example1_en: Rain is likely today.
example1_zh: 今天可能下雨。

meanings_zh: n. 努力 | n. 尝试；有组织的行动
definition_en: hard work | an attempt or organised activity intended to achieve a goal
example1_en: Success needs continuous effort.
example1_zh: 成功需要持续努力。
example2_en: Reducing household waste requires a joint effort from consumers, manufacturers and local authorities to change everyday practices.
example2_zh: 减少家庭垃圾需要消费者、制造商和地方政府共同努力，改变日常做法。
collocations: make an effort｜作出努力 ; put effort into｜投入精力于 ; a joint effort｜共同努力 ; considerable effort｜相当大的努力
tip_zh: 表示精力时不可数；表示一次尝试时可数。

definition_en: in a short time
example1_en: The meeting will start soon.
example1_zh: 会议很快就要开始。
example2_en: A leaking roof will soon damage books if a school waits for a perfect budget.
example2_zh: 如果学校一直等一份完美的预算，漏雨的屋顶很快会损坏书籍。
collocations: as soon as｜一……就 ; sooner or later｜迟早
tip_zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，主句将来时，从句用一般现在时。

definition_en: a piece of a whole, or a role
example1_en: This chapter is the hardest part of the book.
example1_zh: 这一章是书里最难的部分。
example2_en: Parents are only one part of a child's education; streets, screens, and friends shape habits too.
example2_zh: 父母只是孩子教育的一部分；街道、屏幕和朋友也会塑造习惯。
collocations: take part in｜参加 ; play a part｜起作用 ; part of｜……的一部分
tip_zh: take part in 表示参加活动，不要漏掉 in。

definition_en: the leader of a country, club, or some universities
example1_en: The club president will speak first.
example1_zh: 社团主席将首先发言。
example2_en: A student president who only repeats teachers ideas will not represent the class.
example2_zh: 只重复老师想法的学生主席，代表不了班级。
collocations: vice president｜副总统；副主席
tip_zh: president 在不同机构里可以是总统、主席或大学校长。

definition_en: a person's own nature or identity
example1_en: The exercise asks you to describe your self in three words.
example1_zh: 这个练习请你用三个词描述自己。
example2_en: A sense of self grows when students are trusted with real tasks, not only with tests.
example2_zh: 当学生被托付真正的任务而不只是考试时，自我意识会成长。
collocations: self-control｜自制 ; yourself｜你自己
tip_zh: self 常构成复合词，如 self-study。复数是 selves。

meanings_zh: prep. 围绕；大约 | adv. 周围；到处
definition_en: on all sides of, or about | in the surrounding area
example1_en: We walked around the lake after lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭后我们绕着湖走了走。
example2_en: Shops around a school gate affect what students buy between classes, from water to sweets.
example2_zh: 校门口的商店影响着学生课间买什么，从水到糖果都是。
collocations: around the world｜全世界 ; look around｜环顾
tip_zh: around 表示大约时与 about 接近：around 20 students。

definition_en: something accepted as true
example1_en: Strong belief can give people hope.
example1_zh: 坚定的信念能给人希望。
example2_en: The belief that education improves social mobility influences government spending priorities in many countries.
example2_zh: 教育能促进社会流动的这一信念影响着许多国家的政府支出重点。
collocations: belief in someone｜对某人的信任 ; religious beliefs｜宗教信仰 ; a widely held belief｜普遍持有的看法 ; contrary to popular belief｜与普遍看法相反
tip_zh: belief in表示信任或信仰；belief that后接具体看法。

meanings_zh: adj. 小的；少的 | adv. 少
definition_en: small, or not much | not much
example1_en: There is little time before the bus leaves.
example1_zh: 汽车开走前时间不多了。
example2_en: A little shade on a playground can make summer sports safer for younger children.
example2_zh: 操场上一点点荫凉，就能让年幼的孩子在夏天运动时更安全。
collocations: a little｜一点 ; little by little｜逐渐
tip_zh: little 偏否定，表示几乎没有；a little 表示有一点。都修饰不可数名词。

definition_en: the early part of the day
example1_en: I review words every morning.
example1_zh: 我每天早晨复习单词。
example2_en: A hot morning in a room without fans makes the first lesson harder than it needs to be.
example2_zh: 没有风扇的房间里炎热的早晨，会让第一节课难上加难。
collocations: in the morning｜在上午 ; morning exercise｜早操
tip_zh: 泛指上午用 in the morning；具体某一天上午用 on Monday morning。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……外面 | adv. 在外面
definition_en: not inside | outdoors or not inside
example1_en: Please wait outside the office.
example1_zh: 请在办公室外面等。
example2_en: Noise from outside a classroom can undo the quiet a teacher is trying to keep.
example2_zh: 教室外面的噪音可以毁掉老师试图保持的安静。
collocations: outside of｜在……外面
tip_zh: outside 可作介词或副词。

meanings_zh: adj. 黑色的 | n. 黑色
definition_en: of the darkest colour | the colour black
example1_en: The black cat slept on the warm step.
example1_zh: 黑猫睡在温暖的台阶上。
example2_en: Black smoke from old buses is a daily health problem for students waiting at the stop.
example2_zh: 旧公交冒出的黑烟，是等车学生每天面对的健康问题。
collocations: black and white｜黑白的
tip_zh: black 也可作名词表示黑色。

definition_en: of the kind already mentioned
example1_en: I have never seen such a clear night sky.
example1_zh: 我从没见过这么晴朗的夜空。
example2_en: Such a small tax on plastic bags can change what millions of shoppers carry home.
example2_zh: 对塑料袋征收如此小的一笔费用，就能改变数百万人拎回家的东西。
collocations: such as｜例如 ; such...that｜如此……以至于
tip_zh: such a/an + 形容词 + 可数名词单数；so + 形容词。

definition_en: to give information to someone, or to recognise a difference
example1_en: Please tell me when the meeting starts.
example1_zh: 请告诉我会议什么时候开始。
example2_en: A label should tell shoppers where food comes from, not only how attractive the packet looks.
example2_zh: 标签应该告诉购物者食物来自哪里，而不只是包装有多好看。
collocations: tell sb to do｜叫某人做 ; tell...from｜把……与……区分 ; tell a story｜讲故事
tip_zh: tell 后面接人：tell sb sth。say 后面接说的内容，不直接接人。

definition_en: a series of lessons, or the way something develops
example1_en: I chose a history course this term.
example1_zh: 这学期我选了一门历史课。
example2_en: Of course a new course needs books, but it also needs a teacher who has time to mark them.
example2_zh: 新课程当然需要书，但也需要有时间批改的老师。
collocations: of course｜当然 ; in the course of｜在……过程中
tip_zh: course 表示课程；of course 是固定短语“当然”。

definition_en: to make someone believe
example1_en: She tried to convince him to stay.
example1_zh: 她试图说服他留下来。
example2_en: Governments must convince residents that improved public transport offers a practical alternative to private cars.
example2_zh: 政府必须让居民相信，改善后的公共交通能够切实替代私家车出行。
collocations: convince someone of something｜使某人相信某事 ; convince someone that｜使某人确信 ; convince someone to do something｜说服某人做某事
tip_zh: convince sb of sth表示使某人相信某事。

meanings_zh: v. 希望 | n. 希望
definition_en: to want something to happen | a feeling of wanting something good
example1_en: I hope to see you at the concert.
example1_zh: 我希望在音乐会上见到你。
example2_en: Families hope the new clinic will open before winter, when travel on icy roads is harder.
example2_zh: 家人希望新诊所在冬天前开业，因为结冰的路更难走。
collocations: hope to do｜希望做 ; hope for｜希望得到 ; in the hope of｜抱着……的希望
tip_zh: hope 后接 to do 或 that 从句，不说 hope sb to do。

meanings_zh: v. 要求 | n. 坚决要求 | v. 强烈要求；需要
definition_en: to ask for firmly | a strong request that someone expects to be obeyed | to insist on receiving something or require something essential
example1_en: Workers demand better pay and safety.
example1_zh: 工人们要求更好的薪酬和安全。
example2_en: Growing demand for affordable housing has encouraged local authorities to convert unused office buildings into residential accommodation.
example2_zh: 对可负担住房不断增长的需求促使地方政府将闲置办公楼改建为住宅。
collocations: demand for housing｜住房需求 ; meet demand｜满足需求 ; in high demand｜需求旺盛 ; demand an explanation｜要求解释
tip_zh: 要求做某事用demand to do，不用demand sb to do。

meanings_zh: n. 脸；面 | v. 面对
definition_en: the front of the head | to deal with a difficult situation
example1_en: She had a smile on her face.
example1_zh: 她脸上带着微笑。
example2_en: A city must face the fact that cheap housing and clean air are both necessary.
example2_zh: 一座城市必须面对这个事实：廉价住房和干净空气都是必需的。
collocations: face to face｜面对面 ; make a face｜做鬼脸 ; lose face｜丢脸
tip_zh: face 作动词表示面对：face a problem，不要说 face to a problem。

meanings_zh: v. 承认；准许进入 | v. 准许进入；接收
definition_en: to say something is true; to allow in | to allow someone to enter or join a place or institution
example1_en: He had to admit that he was wrong.
example1_zh: 他不得不承认自己错了。
example2_en: Governments should admit when policies have failed and use reliable evidence to develop more effective alternatives.
example2_zh: 政府应承认政策失败，并依据可靠证据制定更有效的替代方案。
collocations: admit a mistake｜承认错误 ; admit doing something｜承认做过某事 ; admit that｜承认…… ; be admitted to hospital｜被收治入院
tip_zh: 用admit doing，不用admit to do；过去式双写t。

definition_en: to make known publicly
example1_en: The teacher will announce the exam date tomorrow.
example1_zh: 老师明天会宣布考试日期。
example2_en: Local authorities should announce major policy changes early so residents have enough time to prepare.
example2_zh: 地方政府应尽早公布重大政策调整，让居民有充足的准备时间。
collocations: announce plans｜宣布计划 ; announce a decision｜宣布决定 ; announce the results｜公布结果
tip_zh: 用announce sth或announce that，不用announce sb sth。

definition_en: a way for vehicles
example1_en: The road to the museum is closed today.
example1_zh: 去博物馆的路今天封闭。
example2_en: A wider road can invite more cars unless buses and bikes are given space too.
example2_zh: 更宽的路会招来更多汽车，除非公交和自行车也有空间。
collocations: on the road｜在路上 ; main road｜主干道
tip_zh: road 多指车辆道路；street 多指两边有建筑的街道。

definition_en: help given to people, or a public system
example1_en: The bus service stops at ten.
example1_zh: 公交服务十点结束。
example2_en: A health service that only works in the city centre leaves villages waiting for basic care.
example2_zh: 只在市中心运转的医疗服务，会让乡村等待基本的照料。
collocations: public service｜公共服务 ; service industry｜服务业
tip_zh: service 表示服务时常不可数；一项具体服务有时用 a service。

definition_en: the end of life
example1_en: The story ends with the death of the old tree.
example1_zh: 故事以那棵老树的死亡结束。
example2_en: Heat-related death is more common in neighbourhoods with little shade and few clinics.
example2_zh: 与高温有关的死亡，在少荫凉、少诊所的社区更常见。
collocations: the death of｜……的死亡
tip_zh: death 是名词；die 是动词；dead 是形容词。

definition_en: the making of beautiful or expressive things
example1_en: There is an art show in the hall.
example1_zh: 大厅里有一场艺术展。
example2_en: Public art on a dull wall can make a walk to school feel shorter and safer.
example2_zh: 单调墙上的公共艺术，能让走路上学感觉更短、更安全。
collocations: work of art｜艺术品 ; art museum｜美术馆
tip_zh: art 泛指艺术时不可数。the arts 可指多种艺术。

meanings_zh: adj. 免费的；空闲的；自由的
definition_en: costing nothing, or not busy, or not controlled
example1_en: Are you free after class today?
example1_zh: 你今天课后有空吗？
example2_en: Free entry to museums matters most to families who would not pay for a ticket.
example2_zh: 博物馆免费入场，对那些本来不会买票的家庭最为重要。
collocations: for free｜免费 ; free time｜空闲时间 ; set free｜释放
tip_zh: free 表示免费或有空；freely 才是副词“自由地”。

definition_en: used to contrast with what was just said
example1_en: The plan is costly. However, it may save water.
example1_zh: 这个计划花费很大。然而，它也许能节水。
example2_en: The museum is free. However, families who live an hour away still pay for the bus.
example2_zh: 博物馆是免费的。然而，住在一小时车程外的家庭仍然要付公交费。
collocations: however hard｜无论多么努力
tip_zh: however 是副词，前后常用句号或分号；but 是连词，连接两个分句。

definition_en: a female parent
example1_en: My mother works at the hospital.
example1_zh: 我母亲在医院工作。
example2_en: A mother on a night shift needs the school to understand why her child sometimes arrives tired.
example2_zh: 上夜班的母亲需要学校理解她的孩子为什么有时疲惫地到校。
collocations: mother tongue｜母语
tip_zh: mother 较正式；mum 或 mom 更口语。

meanings_zh: v. 玩；演奏；参加比赛 | n. 戏剧；比赛
definition_en: to take part in a game, or to perform music | a piece of writing for the theatre, or a game
example1_en: We play basketball after school.
example1_zh: 我们放学后打篮球。
example2_en: Children who play outside learn to judge risk in a way that a screen cannot teach.
example2_zh: 在户外玩耍的孩子会学习判断风险，这是屏幕教不会的。
collocations: play a role｜起作用 ; play the piano｜弹钢琴 ; play with｜玩耍
tip_zh: 球类前不加 the：play football；乐器前加 the：play the violin。

meanings_zh: v. 打架；斗争 | n. 打架；斗争
definition_en: to use force, or to try hard to stop something | a struggle
example1_en: We should not fight in the corridor.
example1_zh: 我们不该在走廊里打架。
example2_en: Communities fight flooding with drains and trees, not only with photos after the water has gone.
example2_zh: 社区用排水和树木对抗洪水，而不只是在水退后拍照。
collocations: fight against｜与……斗争 ; fight for｜为……而战
tip_zh: fight 的过去式和过去分词是 fought。

definition_en: to take air in and out
example1_en: It is hard to breathe in heavy smoke.
example1_zh: 浓烟中很难呼吸。
example2_en: People living near busy roads often breathe polluted air, which can increase their risk of respiratory illness.
example2_zh: 住在繁忙道路附近的人经常吸入受污染的空气，这可能增加他们患呼吸系统疾病的风险。
collocations: breathe deeply｜深呼吸 ; breathe in｜吸气 ; breathe out｜呼气 ; breathe fresh air｜呼吸新鲜空气
tip_zh: breathe是动词，末音/ð/；breath是名词，末音/θ/。

meanings_zh: adj. 白色的 | n. 白色
definition_en: of the colour of snow | the colour white
example1_en: Write your name on the white card.
example1_zh: 把名字写在白色卡片上。
example2_en: White roofs can reflect summer heat and make classrooms easier to cool.
example2_zh: 白色屋顶能反射夏日热量，让教室更容易降温。
collocations: white hair｜白发
tip_zh: white 也可作名词，表示白色。

definition_en: big in size or amount
example1_en: We need a large table for the maps.
example1_zh: 我们需要一张大桌子放地图。
example2_en: A large school on the edge of town forces many children into long bus rides.
example2_zh: 城边的大学校会迫使许多孩子长时间乘公交。
collocations: a large number of｜许多 ; at large｜未被捕；普遍
tip_zh: large 比 big 更正式，常修饰数量和面积。

definition_en: containing as much as possible, or complete
example1_en: The bus was full, so we waited for the next one.
example1_zh: 公交车满了，所以我们等下一辆。
example2_en: A diary full of small observations can later explain how a neighbourhood changed year by year.
example2_zh: 记满细小观察的日记，日后可以解释一个社区如何逐年变化。
collocations: be full of｜充满 ; full name｜全名
tip_zh: be full of 表示充满；fill 是动词“装满”。

meanings_zh: adj. 诚实的 | adj. 坦率的；真诚的
definition_en: truthful | Expressing what you really think or feel.
example1_en: Be honest about your mistakes.
example1_zh: 对自己的错误要诚实。
example2_en: Honest communication between teachers and parents can help schools address students' difficulties before they become serious.
example2_zh: 教师与家长之间坦诚的沟通能帮助学校在学生的问题变得严重之前加以解决。
collocations: an honest person｜诚实的人 ; an honest answer｜坦率的回答 ; to be honest｜说实话
tip_zh: h不发音，因此说an honest person。

definition_en: a figure, or a quantity
example1_en: Write your seat number in the corner.
example1_zh: 把座位号写在角落里。
example2_en: The number of cars has grown faster than the number of safe places for children to cross.
example2_zh: 汽车数量的增长，快过儿童安全过街地点的增长。
collocations: a number of｜许多 ; the number of｜……的数量 ; phone number｜电话号码
tip_zh: a number of 作主语时谓语常用复数；the number of 作主语时谓语用单数。

meanings_zh: v. 损害；毁坏 | v. 损坏；损害
definition_en: to harm | Harm something or make it less effective.
example1_en: Floods can damage houses and roads.
example1_zh: 洪水会毁坏房屋和道路。
example2_en: Uncontrolled tourism can damage fragile ecosystems and reduce the quality of life for local residents.
example2_zh: 不受控制的旅游活动可能破坏脆弱的生态系统，并降低当地居民的生活质量。
collocations: cause damage｜造成损害 ; damage to property｜财产损坏 ; environmental damage｜环境破坏 ; damage someone's reputation｜损害某人的声誉
tip_zh: 损害用不可数damage；damages指法律赔偿金。

definition_en: thankful
example1_en: I am grateful for your help.
example1_zh: 我感激你的帮助。
example2_en: Many students are grateful for scholarships that allow them to continue their education despite financial difficulties.
example2_zh: 许多学生感谢奖学金让他们即使经济困难也能继续学业。
collocations: grateful to someone｜感激某人 ; grateful for something｜感谢某事 ; deeply grateful｜深表感激
tip_zh: be grateful to某人 for某事；注意不是greatful。

definition_en: at any time
example1_en: Have you ever visited the city museum?
example1_zh: 你去过市博物馆吗？
example2_en: If a river has ever flooded the same street twice, planners should stop building basements there.
example2_zh: 如果一条河曾两次淹没同一条街，规划者就不该再在那里建地下室。
collocations: for ever｜永远 ; ever since｜自从
tip_zh: ever 常用于疑问句和否定句；肯定句里的“曾经”多用 once。

definition_en: in place of something else
example1_en: We walked instead of taking the bus.
example1_zh: 我们没有坐公交，而是走路。
example2_en: Planting trees instead of only widening roads can cool a street and slow the rain.
example2_zh: 种树而不是只拓宽道路，可以给街道降温，并减缓雨水。
collocations: instead of｜而不是
tip_zh: instead 可放句首或句末；instead of 后接名词或 doing。

definition_en: used for obligation or a strong guess
example1_en: You must wear glasses in the lab.
example1_zh: 在实验室里你必须戴眼镜。
example2_en: A public promise must be followed by a date and a person responsible, or it is only a sentence.
example2_zh: 一项公开承诺必须跟上日期和负责人，否则就只是一句话。
collocations: must be｜一定是 ; must not｜禁止
tip_zh: must not 表示禁止；不必是 don't have to 或 needn't。

meanings_zh: adj. 简短的 | v. 向……介绍情况 | n. 任务说明；工作要求
definition_en: short in time or words | To give someone essential information or instructions. | Instructions explaining what a task should achieve.
example1_en: Give a brief summary.
example1_zh: 做个简短总结。
example2_en: Teachers should brief students on safety procedures before allowing them to conduct experiments independently.
example2_zh: 教师应先向学生介绍安全操作规程，再允许他们独立进行实验。
collocations: a brief summary｜简要总结 ; a brief pause｜短暂停顿 ; brief someone on｜向某人介绍……的情况 ; a design brief｜设计任务说明
tip_zh: brief指时间短或内容简洁，本身不表示草率。

definition_en: each one in a group, seen as a whole
example1_en: Every student has a chance to speak.
example1_zh: 每个学生都有发言的机会。
example2_en: Every extra degree of summer heat makes it harder to keep classrooms comfortable without more energy.
example2_zh: 夏天每升高一度，都让教室在不增加能耗的情况下更难保持舒适。
collocations: every day｜每天 ; every other day｜每隔一天
tip_zh: every 后接单数名词；every day 是短语，everyday 是形容词“日常的”。

definition_en: to some degree, or completely
example1_en: The room is quite quiet after four.
example1_zh: 四点以后房间相当安静。
example2_en: A cycle lane that is quite short still helps if it crosses the most dangerous junction.
example2_zh: 一段相当短的自行车道，如果穿过最危险的路口，仍然有帮助。
collocations: quite a few｜不少 ; quite a lot｜相当多
tip_zh: quite a + 形容词 + 名词：quite a long walk。不说 a quite long walk。

definition_en: something that is known to be true
example1_en: In fact, the library opens at eight.
example1_zh: 事实上，图书馆八点开门。
example2_en: A fact about air pollution should be separated from an opinion about who is to blame.
example2_zh: 关于空气污染的事实，应该和谁该受责备的看法分开。
collocations: in fact｜事实上 ; as a matter of fact｜事实上
tip_zh: fact 是可数名词。the fact that 后接从句。

definition_en: pleasant or kind
example1_en: It was nice of you to wait for me.
example1_zh: 你等我，真是太好了。
example2_en: A nice park on a map is not enough if the path to it is dark and unsafe at night.
example2_zh: 地图上一个好看的公园不够，如果去那里的路夜里又黑又不安全。
collocations: be nice to｜对……友好 ; nice and｜很
tip_zh: It is nice of sb to do 表扬某人的善意。

definition_en: having a big effect or value
example1_en: It is important to write the date on the form.
example1_zh: 在表格上写日期很重要。
example2_en: Clean drinking water is more important to a growing town than another bright shopping sign.
example2_zh: 对一个发展中的城镇来说，干净的饮用水比又一块闪亮的商店招牌更重要。
collocations: be important to｜对……重要 ; more important｜更重要
tip_zh: It is important for sb to do，不要漏掉 for 或 to。

meanings_zh: v. 行进；游行 | n. 行进；三月（March）
definition_en: to walk with regular steps, often in a group | a walk by a group, or the third month when capitalised
example1_en: The band will march onto the field.
example1_zh: 乐队将列队走上场地。
example2_en: People march when a decision about their street is made without asking them.
example2_zh: 当关于他们街道的决定没有询问他们就做出时，人们会游行。
collocations: on the march｜在行进中
tip_zh: March 大写是三月；march 小写是行进。不要在句子里混用大小写。

meanings_zh: v. 支持；供养 | n. 支持
definition_en: to agree with and help, or to provide what is needed | help or approval
example1_en: Our class supports the book-sharing plan.
example1_zh: 我们班支持图书共享计划。
example2_en: Parents cannot support a long school day if the buses stop before the last lesson ends.
example2_zh: 如果公交车在最后一节课结束前就停运，父母就无法支持过长的在校时间。
collocations: in support of｜支持 ; support sb in｜在某方面支持
tip_zh: support 是及物动词，后面直接接宾语，不加 to。

definition_en: a building where people live
example1_en: Their house is next to the post office.
example1_zh: 他们的房子在邮局旁边。
example2_en: A house built on cheap wetland may cost less at first and much more after the first flood.
example2_zh: 建在廉价湿地上的房子，起初可能更便宜，第一次洪水之后却贵得多。
collocations: housewife｜家庭主妇 ; in the house｜在房子里
tip_zh: house 是建筑物；home 是家的感觉或所在。

definition_en: to decide after thinking; to end
example1_en: We can conclude that practice helps.
example1_zh: 我们可以得出结论：练习有帮助。

meanings_zh: v. 影响 | v. 使感动；使悲伤
definition_en: to have an influence on | to cause someone to feel a strong emotion
example1_en: Noise can affect your ability to sleep.
example1_zh: 噪音会影响你的睡眠能力。
example2_en: Rising food prices disproportionately affect poorer households, which spend a larger share of their income on essentials.
example2_zh: 食品价格上涨对较贫困家庭的影响尤为严重，因为必需品支出占其收入的比例更大。
collocations: affect health｜影响健康 ; adversely affect｜产生不利影响 ; deeply affect someone｜深深触动某人 ; affect performance｜影响表现
tip_zh: 表示“影响”时affect是动词，effect通常是名词。

definition_en: a place where people buy and sell
example1_en: We buy fruit at the morning market.
example1_zh: 我们在早市买水果。
example2_en: A local market keeps money in the town, while a distant supermarket sends it away.
example2_zh: 本地市场把钱留在镇上，而远处的超市把钱送走。
collocations: on the market｜在出售 ; market price｜市场价格
tip_zh: market 作动词是“推销”。

meanings_zh: n. 优势；有利条件 | n. 好处；益处
definition_en: something that helps you | A useful or positive feature of something.
example1_en: Speaking two languages is an advantage.
example1_zh: 会说两种语言是一种优势。
example2_en: One major advantage of public transport is its ability to reduce traffic congestion in urban areas.
example2_zh: 公共交通的一大好处是能够缓解城市地区的交通拥堵。
collocations: competitive advantage｜竞争优势 ; have an advantage over｜比……有优势 ; take advantage of｜利用；占……便宜 ; a major advantage｜一大优势
tip_zh: take advantage of可指利用机会，也可指占人便宜。

meanings_zh: adj. 晚的；迟到的 | adv. 晚
definition_en: after the expected time | after the right time
example1_en: I was late because the bus did not come.
example1_zh: 我迟到了，因为公交没来。
example2_en: Late buses leave students waiting in the dark, which is a safety problem as well as a delay.
example2_zh: 晚点的公交让学生在黑暗中等待，这既是延误，也是安全问题。
collocations: be late for｜……迟到 ; later on｜后来
tip_zh: late 可作形容词或副词。lately 是“最近”，不是“迟到地”。

definition_en: how old someone is, or a period of history
example1_en: What is the age of the oldest student in the club?
example1_zh: 社团里年龄最大的学生几岁？
example2_en: In an age of cheap photos, it is harder to know which picture shows a real event.
example2_zh: 在照片便宜的时代，更难知道哪张照片展示的是真事。
collocations: at the age of｜在……岁时 ; for ages｜很久
tip_zh: at the age of 后接数字。同龄用 of the same age。

meanings_zh: v. 收费；充电；指控 | n. 费用；收费 | v. 给……充电
definition_en: to ask for money; to accuse | An amount of money requested for goods or services. | Put electrical energy into a battery or device.
example1_en: Hotels often charge extra for breakfast.
example1_zh: 酒店常对早餐额外收费。
example2_en: Museums that charge admission fees should offer discounts to ensure that students can still access cultural resources.
example2_zh: 收取门票的博物馆应提供优惠，以确保学生仍能享用文化资源。
collocations: charge a fee｜收取费用 ; free of charge｜免费 ; charge a battery｜给电池充电 ; in charge of｜负责；掌管
tip_zh: 向某人收取某项费用：charge someone for something。

meanings_zh: v. 意思是；意味着 | adj. 吝啬的；刻薄的
definition_en: to have a particular meaning, or to intend | not generous, or unkind
example1_en: What does this word mean in the passage?
example1_zh: 这个词在文章里是什么意思？
example2_en: A low score does not mean a student cannot learn; it may mean the test ignored what they can do.
example2_zh: 低分并不意味着学生学不会；它可能意味着考试忽略了他们会做的事。
collocations: mean to do｜打算做 ; mean doing｜意味着 ; I mean｜我的意思是
tip_zh: mean to do 是打算；mean doing 是意味着。

meanings_zh: v. 打开；开业 | adj. 开着的；公开的
definition_en: to make something not closed, or to start a business | not closed, or public
example1_en: Open the window if the room feels hot.
example1_zh: 如果房间闷，就把窗户打开。
example2_en: Shops that open late help workers who cannot buy food before their shift ends.
example2_zh: 营业到很晚的商店，帮助那些下班前买不到食物的工人。
collocations: open up｜打开；开创 ; in the open｜在户外
tip_zh: open 作形容词是“开着的”；be open 表示状态，不要说 be opened 表示日常开着。

definition_en: matching the facts
example1_en: Is it true that the museum is free today?
example1_zh: 博物馆今天免费，这是真的吗？
example2_en: A story can sound true and still leave out the people who were harmed.
example2_zh: 一个故事可以听起来真实，却仍然漏掉受到伤害的人。
collocations: come true｜实现 ; true to｜忠实于
tip_zh: come true 的主语是梦想或预言，不用被动。true 强调符合事实。

meanings_zh: n. 交易；数量 | v. 处理；交易
definition_en: an agreement, or an amount | to handle, or to do business
example1_en: We made a deal to share the cleaning.
example1_zh: 我们说好轮流打扫。
example2_en: A great deal of plastic leaves a school every day if the canteen still uses single-use boxes.
example2_zh: 如果食堂仍用一次性盒子，学校每天都会送出大量塑料。
collocations: a great deal of｜大量 ; deal with｜处理 ; a good deal｜相当多
tip_zh: a great deal of 后接不可数名词。deal with 表示处理。

definition_en: a way of doing something
example1_en: The bus is our only means of getting to the museum.
example1_zh: 公交是我们去博物馆的唯一办法。
example2_en: A means of checking news matters when a false photo can travel faster than a correction.
example2_zh: 当一张假照片比更正传得更快时，核对新闻的方法就很重要。
collocations: by means of｜凭借 ; by all means｜当然可以 ; by no means｜决不
tip_zh: means 单复数同形。a means 是一种方法，谓语用单数。

meanings_zh: adj. 公共的；公开的 | n. 公众
definition_en: for everyone, or known to people in general | people in general
example1_en: The public library is open on Sundays.
example1_zh: 公共图书馆周日开放。
example2_en: Public money should be easy to trace, from the tax office to the classroom it is meant to support.
example2_zh: 公共资金应该易于追踪，从税务部门一直到它本应支持的教室。
collocations: in public｜公开地 ; public transport｜公共交通 ; the public｜公众
tip_zh: the public 表示公众，谓语常用单数。

definition_en: a way of thinking or feeling
example1_en: A positive attitude helps in hard times.
example1_zh: 积极态度有助于渡过难关。
example2_en: Schools can encourage a positive attitude towards learning by giving students constructive feedback rather than constant criticism.
example2_zh: 学校可以给予学生建设性的反馈，而非不断批评，以培养积极的学习态度。
collocations: positive attitude｜积极的态度 ; attitude towards｜对……的态度 ; change of attitude｜态度的转变 ; public attitudes｜公众态度
tip_zh: 对某事的态度常用attitude to或towards。

definition_en: any person
example1_en: Anyone can borrow books with a library card.
example1_zh: 任何人有借书证都可以借书。
example2_en: Anyone planning a new road should ask the people who will walk beside it every day.
example2_zh: 任何计划修新路的人，都应该问问每天要在路边走的人。
collocations: anyone else｜其他任何人
tip_zh: anyone 作主语时谓语用单数。疑问句和否定句比 someone 更常见。

definition_en: a situation, a legal matter, or a container
example1_en: In this case, we should ask the teacher.
example1_zh: 在这种情况下，我们应该问老师。
example2_en: In the case of a city flood, the first question is which roads still lead to the hospital.
example2_zh: 如果城市内涝，第一个问题是哪些路仍然通向医院。
collocations: in case｜以防万一 ; in case of｜如果发生 ; in any case｜无论如何
tip_zh: in case 后接句子，表示以防万一；in case of 后接名词。

definition_en: a number of people or things together
example1_en: Our group will present first.
example1_zh: 我们组第一个展示。
example2_en: A small group of volunteers can keep a community library open when the town budget is thin.
example2_zh: 当城镇预算紧张时，一小群志愿者也能维持社区图书馆开放。
collocations: a group of｜一群 ; group work｜小组活动
tip_zh: a group of 加复数名词时，谓语可随强调整体或成员而变化。

meanings_zh: conj. 当……时；而 | n. 一会儿
definition_en: during the time that, or whereas | a period of time
example1_en: I listened to the recording while I washed the dishes.
example1_zh: 我洗碗时听了录音。
example2_en: Some cities invest in stadiums while their oldest school buildings still leak in the rain.
example2_zh: 一些城市投资体育场，而它们最老的校舍下雨时仍在漏水。
collocations: for a while｜一会儿 ; once in a while｜偶尔
tip_zh: while 可表示对比，相当于“而”；一段时间用 for a while。

definition_en: a place where children are educated
example1_en: Our school has a new science lab.
example1_zh: 我们学校有一间新的科学实验室。
example2_en: A school that stays open in the evening can give working parents a safe place for their children.
example2_zh: 晚上仍然开放的学校，可以为上班的父母提供一个孩子的安全去处。
collocations: at school｜在上学 ; go to school｜去上学 ; primary school｜小学
tip_zh: go to school 泛指上学，school 前通常不加 the。

meanings_zh: v. 放置；设置；确立 | n. 一套；集合
definition_en: to put, arrange, or establish | a group of things that belong together
example1_en: Please set the chairs in a circle.
example1_zh: 请把椅子摆成一圈。
example2_en: If a school sets homework without time to sleep, the extra pages may lower the next day's attention.
example2_zh: 如果学校布置的作业挤掉了睡眠，多出来的页数可能会降低第二天的注意力。
collocations: set up｜建立 ; set off｜出发 ; a set of｜一套
tip_zh: set 的过去式和过去分词都是 set。a set of 后接复数名词。

definition_en: at all times
example1_en: She always checks her answers twice.
example1_zh: 她总是把答案检查两遍。
example2_en: Towns that always build on the cheapest land may later discover that the ground floods.
example2_zh: 总在最便宜的土地上建设的城镇，日后可能会发现那块地会积水。
collocations: always remember｜永远记得
tip_zh: always 放在实义动词前、be 动词后。

definition_en: past events, or the study of them
example1_en: We have a history test on Friday.
example1_zh: 我们周五有历史测验。
example2_en: Local history is easier to care about when students can visit the street the textbook describes.
example2_zh: 当学生能去教科书描写的那条街时，本地历史就更容易让人在意。
collocations: in history｜在历史上 ; history museum｜历史博物馆
tip_zh: history 作学科不可数。historical 是“历史的”；historic 常指有历史意义的。

meanings_zh: n. 影响；效果 | v. 实现；使发生
definition_en: a result | To bring about a change or result.
example1_en: Sleep has a strong effect on mood.
example1_zh: 睡眠对情绪有强烈影响。
example2_en: Higher parking charges may have little effect on traffic unless reliable public transport is also available.
example2_zh: 如果没有可靠的公共交通，提高停车费对交通状况的影响可能很小。
collocations: have an effect on｜对……有影响 ; side effect｜副作用 ; take effect｜生效；起作用 ; effect change｜促成变革
tip_zh: effect常作名词；affect常作动词，意为影响。

definition_en: a part of a place, or the size of a surface
example1_en: This area of the library is for quiet study.
example1_zh: 图书馆这一区是安静学习用的。
example2_en: Industrial areas beside rivers need stricter rules, because waste travels farther than the factory gate.
example2_zh: 河边的工业区需要更严的规定，因为废物会流到比厂门更远的地方。
collocations: in the area｜在该地区 ; area of｜……的面积
tip_zh: area 可指地区或面积，面积不可数时仍说 an area of。

meanings_zh: v. 申请；应用 | v. 应用；适用 | v. 涂；敷
definition_en: to ask formally; to use | To use something practically, or be relevant to a situation | To spread a substance onto a surface
example1_en: She will apply for a scholarship.
example1_zh: 她将申请奖学金。
example2_en: Universities should encourage students from disadvantaged backgrounds to apply for scholarships that cover tuition and living expenses.
example2_zh: 大学应鼓励家庭条件困难的学生申请涵盖学费和生活费的奖学金。
collocations: apply for a job｜申请工作 ; apply to a university｜向大学提出申请 ; apply knowledge｜应用知识 ; apply sunscreen｜涂防晒霜
tip_zh: apply for接申请事项；apply to接机构或适用对象。

meanings_zh: adj. 立即的 | adj. 速溶的；即食的 | n. 瞬间；片刻
definition_en: happening at once | prepared very quickly, usually by adding hot water | an extremely short period of time
example1_en: She got an instant reply.
example1_zh: 她得到了立即回复。
example2_en: Digital platforms provide instant access to educational resources, although reliable internet connections remain essential.
example2_zh: 数字平台让人们即时获取教育资源，但稳定的网络连接仍然必不可少。
collocations: instant access｜即时获取 ; instant results｜即时结果 ; instant coffee｜速溶咖啡 ; in an instant｜转眼间
tip_zh: instant作形容词表示即时的；in an instant表示转眼间。

meanings_zh: n. 结论；结尾 | n. 结尾；结束
definition_en: a final decision or end | the final part or ending of something
example1_en: The conclusion of the report is clear.
example1_zh: 报告的结论很清楚。
example2_en: Researchers should consider alternative explanations before drawing a conclusion from a relatively small sample.
example2_zh: 研究人员根据较小的样本得出结论之前，应考虑其他可能的解释。
collocations: reach a conclusion｜得出结论 ; draw a conclusion｜作出推断 ; jump to conclusions｜贸然下结论 ; in conclusion｜总而言之
tip_zh: “得出结论”用reach或draw a conclusion，不用make。

definition_en: trade, a company, or a matter to deal with
example1_en: Her aunt runs a small business near the station.
example1_zh: 她阿姨在车站附近做小生意。
example2_en: A business that ignores its waste may save money this year and lose the trust of the town next year.
example2_zh: 忽视废弃物的企业今年也许省了钱，明年却可能失去城镇的信任。
collocations: on business｜出差 ; do business｜做生意 ; none of one's business｜不关某人的事
tip_zh: business 表示生意时可不可数；表示一家企业时可数。

meanings_zh: n. 名字；名称 | v. 命名；说出名字
definition_en: what a person or thing is called | to give a name, or to say a name
example1_en: Please write your name in capital letters.
example1_zh: 请用大写字母写你的名字。
example2_en: A place can lose its old name when new maps care more about roads than about the people who named it.
example2_zh: 当新地图更在意道路而不是命名的人时，一个地方可能失去旧名。
collocations: family name｜姓 ; first name｜名 ; by name｜按名字
tip_zh: name 作动词是“命名”：name the baby。

definition_en: many times
example1_en: I often review new words on the bus.
example1_zh: 我经常在公交上复习生词。
example2_en: Streets that often flood need a better drain, not only a warning after the rain starts.
example2_zh: 经常积水的街道需要更好的排水，而不只是雨开始后的警报。
collocations: how often｜多久一次
tip_zh: often 放在实义动词前、be 动词后。

meanings_zh: n. 目标；目的 | v. 力求；旨在 | v. 瞄准；对准
definition_en: a purpose or goal | to intend or try to achieve something | to point something towards a particular target
example1_en: Our aim is to finish on time.
example1_zh: 我们的目标是按时完成。
example2_en: The programme aims to reduce youth unemployment by providing practical training and opportunities to gain workplace experience.
example2_zh: 该项目旨在通过提供实践培训和获取职场经验的机会，降低青年失业率。
collocations: the main aim｜主要目标 ; aim to do something｜力求做某事 ; with the aim of｜以……为目的 ; aim at a target｜瞄准目标
tip_zh: aim to do表打算做；aim at doing表力求实现。

definition_en: a very young child
example1_en: The baby slept through the whole meeting.
example1_zh: 婴儿在整个会议期间都睡着。
example2_en: A baby clinic once a month is not enough for a village that is two hours from the hospital.
example2_zh: 对离医院两小时的村子来说，每月一次的婴儿诊所是不够的。
collocations: baby boy｜男婴
tip_zh: baby 的复数是 babies。

definition_en: the clear liquid we drink | to pour water on plants
example1_en: Please bring your own water to the sports meet.
example1_zh: 运动会请自带水。
example2_en: When a city wastes water in dry months, farms downstream have less for the next planting season.
example2_zh: 城市在干旱月份浪费水，下游农场下一季可种的水就更少。
collocations: drinking water｜饮用水 ; a glass of water｜一杯水
tip_zh: water 通常不可数，不说 a water。

meanings_zh: n. 一半 | det. 一半的
definition_en: one of two equal parts | equal to one of two parts
example1_en: Half of the class walks to school.
example1_zh: 班上一半的人步行上学。
example2_en: Cutting a journey by half still leaves some students on the bus for more than an hour.
example2_zh: 把路程缩短一半，仍有一些学生要在公交上坐一个多小时。
collocations: half an hour｜半小时 ; in half｜成两半
tip_zh: half of 加复数名词时谓语常用复数；half an hour 中间有 an。

meanings_zh: adj. 复杂的 | n. 综合建筑群
definition_en: having many parts | A group of buildings used for related activities.
example1_en: The problem is more complex than it looks.
example1_zh: 问题比看上去更复杂。
example2_en: Urban poverty is a complex issue that requires cooperation between governments, businesses and local communities.
example2_zh: 城市贫困是一个复杂问题，需要政府、企业和当地社区共同合作。
collocations: complex issue｜复杂问题 ; complex system｜复杂系统 ; sports complex｜综合体育场馆
tip_zh: 作形容词指复杂；作名词可指综合建筑群。

definition_en: in the space or time separating two things
example1_en: The lab is between the library and the hall.
example1_zh: 实验室在图书馆和大厅之间。
example2_en: The difference between knowing a word and using it shows up when students write under time pressure.
example2_zh: 认识一个词和会用一个词的差别，会在学生限时写作时显现出来。
collocations: between...and｜在……和……之间 ; in between｜在中间
tip_zh: between 多用于两者；among 用于三者或更多。

definition_en: at or to a great distance | distant
example1_en: The station is not far from our school.
example1_zh: 车站离我们学校不远。
example2_en: Families who live far from a hospital wait longer when a child is suddenly ill.
example2_zh: 住得离医院远的家庭，孩子突然生病时要等更久。
collocations: far from｜远离 ; so far｜到目前为止 ; as far as｜就……而言
tip_zh: far 的比较级是 farther 或 further；further 还可表示“进一步的”。

definition_en: a well-known statement, or something said
example1_en: There is an old saying about practice.
example1_zh: 有一句关于练习的老话。
example2_en: A saying about saving water means little unless the school itself fixes a leaking tap.
example2_zh: 如果学校自己不修漏水的水龙头，一句关于节水的谚语就没什么意义。
collocations: as the saying goes｜俗话说
tip_zh: saying 也可是 say 的 -ing 形式。作名词“谚语”是可数的。

meanings_zh: n. 要点；点；分数 | v. 指；指向
definition_en: the main idea, a dot, or a score | to show direction with a finger
example1_en: The point of the story is to check your sources.
example1_zh: 这个故事的要点是要核对来源。
example2_en: There is little point in collecting data if nobody is responsible for acting on it.
example2_zh: 如果没有人负责根据数据采取行动，收集数据就没什么意义。
collocations: the point is｜重点是 ; point of view｜观点 ; to the point｜切题
tip_zh: point 作动词是“指”：point at / point to。There is no point in doing 表示做某事没有意义。

definition_en: a business, or the state of being with someone
example1_en: Her mother works for a bus company.
example1_zh: 她母亲在一家公交公司工作。
example2_en: A company that moves its factory should also say what will happen to the workers who stay behind.
example2_zh: 搬迁工厂的公司，也应该说明留下来的工人会怎样。
collocations: keep sb company｜陪伴某人 ; company policy｜公司政策
tip_zh: company 表示陪伴时不可数：for company。表示公司时可数。

meanings_zh: n. 解释 | n. 原因；解释理由
definition_en: words that make something clear | a reason given for why something happened
example1_en: Her explanation helped us understand.
example1_zh: 她的解释帮助我们理解。
example2_en: One possible explanation for declining car ownership is the growing availability of reliable public transport.
example2_zh: 汽车拥有率下降的一个可能原因，是可靠的公共交通越来越普及。
collocations: clear explanation｜清楚的解释 ; give an explanation｜作出解释 ; explanation for｜对……的原因解释 ; explanation of｜对……的说明
tip_zh: explanation of多说明内容，for多解释原因。

definition_en: whole
example1_en: The entire class passed the test.
example1_zh: 整个班级都通过了考试。

meanings_zh: v. 改变；更换 | n. 变化；零钱
definition_en: to become different, or to replace | a difference, or coins returned
example1_en: We changed the time of the meeting.
example1_zh: 我们改了开会时间。
example2_en: Cities that change bus routes without warning leave workers late and children waiting in the dark.
example2_zh: 不预先通知就更改公交线路的城市，会让工人迟到，让孩子在黑暗中等候。
collocations: change into｜变成 ; change one's mind｜改变主意
tip_zh: change 可作及物或不及物动词。

meanings_zh: v. 竞争 | v. 参加比赛
definition_en: to try to win against others | Take part in a sporting event or other contest.
example1_en: Many teams compete for the prize.
example1_zh: 许多队伍竞争这个奖项。
example2_en: Small businesses often struggle to compete with larger companies that can offer lower prices.
example2_zh: 小企业往往难以与能够提供更低价格的大公司竞争。
collocations: compete with｜与……竞争 ; compete for｜争夺 ; compete in a tournament｜参加锦标赛
tip_zh: compete with/against对手；for奖项；in赛事。

definition_en: prepared
example1_en: Are you ready for the listening test?
example1_zh: 听力测试你准备好了吗？
example2_en: A town is not ready for a flood if the only high road is already full of parked cars.
example2_zh: 如果唯一的高路已经停满车，一个城镇就还没有为洪水做好准备。
collocations: be ready to do｜准备好做 ; get ready｜做准备
tip_zh: be ready for 后接名词；be ready to do 后接动词。

meanings_zh: adj. 独立的 | adj. 不受控制的；独立的 | adj. 无关联的；互不影响的
definition_en: not needing others' control | not controlled by another person, organisation, or country | not connected with or affected by something else
example1_en: She became more independent at college.
example1_zh: 她上大学后更独立了。
example2_en: Independent research can help governments assess whether new environmental policies are achieving their intended goals.
example2_zh: 独立研究可以帮助政府评估新的环境政策是否正在实现预期目标。
collocations: financially independent｜经济独立的 ; independent research｜独立研究 ; independent of｜不依赖；不受影响 ; independent judgement｜独立判断
tip_zh: 常搭配of：independent of意为不依赖或不受影响。

definition_en: a thought or plan
example1_en: That is a good idea for the poster.
example1_zh: 对海报来说那是个好主意。
example2_en: An idea for a new park fails if nobody asks who will water the trees after the opening day.
example2_zh: 如果没人问开放日之后谁来给树浇水，建新公园的想法就会失败。
collocations: have no idea｜不知道 ; the idea of｜……的想法
tip_zh: idea 是可数名词：an idea。

meanings_zh: v. 行动；表演 | n. 行为；法令
definition_en: to do something, or to perform | something done, or a law
example1_en: We must act before the river rises again.
example1_zh: 我们必须在河水再次上涨前行动。
example2_en: Schools that act on student suggestions show that those suggestions were not only a form to fill.
example2_zh: 根据学生建议采取行动的学校，表明那些建议不只是一张要填的表。
collocations: act as｜充当 ; act on｜按照……行动
tip_zh: act 强调行动；action 是名词。

definition_en: one of the four parts of the year, or a sports period
example1_en: Autumn is my favourite season.
example1_zh: 秋天是我最喜欢的季节。
example2_en: A long dry season can empty village wells before the next rain arrives.
example2_zh: 漫长的旱季会在下一场雨到来前抽干村里的水井。
collocations: rainy season｜雨季 ; in season｜当令
tip_zh: 季节前常用 in：in summer。

definition_en: towards a lower place
example1_en: Please sit down and open your books.
example1_zh: 请坐下，把书打开。
example2_en: When a factory closes down, the town has to find new work for the people who stayed.
example2_zh: 当一家工厂倒闭时，城镇必须为留下来的人找到新的工作。
collocations: sit down｜坐下 ; write down｜写下 ; up and down｜上上下下
tip_zh: down 可作副词或介词：walk down the street。

definition_en: having the power or skill to do something
example1_en: She is able to explain the diagram clearly.
example1_zh: 她能把这张图讲清楚。
example2_en: Students are more able to concentrate when the classroom is quiet and the air is fresh.
example2_zh: 当教室安静、空气新鲜时，学生更能集中注意力。
collocations: be able to｜能够 ; able student｜有能力的学生
tip_zh: can 多指一般能力；be able to 可用于各种时态，并强调做成。

meanings_zh: n. 焦点；重点 | n. 重点；关注中心 | n. 清晰度；焦点
definition_en: the center of attention | the main subject receiving attention or effort | image sharpness, or the point where light rays meet
example1_en: Keep your focus on the task.
example1_zh: 把注意力集中在任务上。
example2_en: Governments should focus on affordable public transport to reduce congestion and improve access to employment.
example2_zh: 政府应重点发展价格合理的公共交通，以缓解拥堵并改善就业机会的可达性。
collocations: focus on｜集中于 ; the main focus｜主要关注点 ; in focus｜影像清晰 ; out of focus｜影像模糊
tip_zh: focus on后接名词或动名词；不要说focus in。

meanings_zh: adj. 红色的 | n. 红色
definition_en: of the colour of blood | the colour red
example1_en: The red bag on the chair is mine.
example1_zh: 椅子上的红包是我的。
example2_en: Red warnings on a river app help only if people who live nearby can actually receive them.
example2_zh: 河流应用上的红色警报只有在附近居民真能收到时才有用。
collocations: red light｜红灯
tip_zh: red 也可作名词表示红色。

definition_en: to carry something towards the speaker
example1_en: Please bring your student card tomorrow.
example1_zh: 请明天带学生证。
example2_en: New jobs bring people to a town only if there is also a place for them to live.
example2_zh: 只有同时有地方住，新工作才会把人带到一个城镇。
collocations: bring about｜引起 ; bring up｜抚养；提出
tip_zh: bring 是带来（朝说话人）；take 是带走。过去式是 brought。

definition_en: why something happens
example1_en: The reason for the delay was the rain.
example1_zh: 延误的原因是下雨。
example2_en: The reason a street floods is often an old drain, not only a heavy cloud.
example2_zh: 街道积水的原因常常是旧排水管，而不只是厚云。
collocations: the reason for｜……的原因 ; the reason why｜……的原因
tip_zh: the reason 后用 why 或 that，不要再用 because 重复原因。

meanings_zh: adj. 频繁的 | v. 常去；常到访
definition_en: happening often | Visit a particular place regularly
example1_en: frequent rain delayed the flight.
example1_zh: 频繁的降雨延误了航班。
example2_en: Frequent changes in education policy can make it difficult for teachers to plan effective lessons.
example2_zh: 教育政策频繁变化，可能使教师难以规划有效的课堂教学。
collocations: frequent visits｜频繁到访 ; frequent delays｜频繁延误 ; a frequent visitor｜常客 ; frequent changes｜频繁变化
tip_zh: 形容词重音在首音节；动词重音在第二音节。

meanings_zh: n. 结尾；末端 | v. 结束
definition_en: the last part of something | to finish
example1_en: Please write your name at the end of the page.
example1_zh: 请把名字写在页尾。
example2_en: The end of a holiday is a good time to ask which local shops actually benefited from the visitors.
example2_zh: 假期结束时，适合问问哪些本地店铺真正从游客那里获益。
collocations: in the end｜最后 ; at the end of｜在……末尾 ; end up｜最终成为
tip_zh: in the end 表示最终；at the end of 后面要接具体的时间或事物。

definition_en: to begin to be
example1_en: The room will become quiet when the talk starts.
example1_zh: 讲座开始时房间会安静下来。
example2_en: A neighbourhood can become unsafe for walking if shops close and the street lights fail.
example2_zh: 如果商店关门、路灯不亮，一个社区会变得不适合步行。
collocations: become of｜发生……情况
tip_zh: become 后接形容词或名词，不加 to be。过去分词仍是 become。

definition_en: the earth, or a particular area of activity
example1_en: Students from three countries joined the world map project.
example1_zh: 来自三个国家的学生参加了世界地图项目。
example2_en: The online world gives teenagers a voice, but it also spreads rumours faster than a classroom can correct them.
example2_zh: 网络世界给了青少年发言的机会，但谣言传播的速度也快过课堂能够纠正的速度。
collocations: all over the world｜全世界 ; in the world｜在世界上
tip_zh: in the world 常与最高级连用，加强语气。

meanings_zh: n. 南；南方 | adj. 南方的
definition_en: the direction opposite north | in or towards the south
example1_en: The library is to the south of the stadium.
example1_zh: 图书馆在体育馆南边。
example2_en: Towns in the south may face longer summers, which changes when schools can hold sports outdoors.
example2_zh: 南方的城镇可能面临更长的夏天，这会改变学校何时能在户外运动。
collocations: in the south｜在南方 ; South Africa｜南非
tip_zh: in the south of 表示在某范围的南部；to the south of 表示在某地以南。

definition_en: fairly, or preferably
example1_en: The question is rather difficult.
example1_zh: 这道题相当难。
example2_en: Many students would rather walk than take a bus that arrives after the gate has closed.
example2_zh: 许多学生宁愿走路，也不愿坐一辆校门关上后才到的公交。
collocations: rather than｜而不是 ; would rather｜宁愿
tip_zh: would rather do than do 表示宁愿……而不愿。rather than 后常接不带 to 的动词。

definition_en: knowing about something
example1_en: Be aware of the risks.
example1_zh: 要意识到风险。

meanings_zh: v. 结合；联合 | n. 联合收割机
definition_en: to join together | A farm machine that harvests grain and separates the seeds.
example1_en: Good teachers combine hard work with creativity.
example1_zh: 好老师把努力与创造力结合起来。
example2_en: Cities can combine improved public transport with safer cycling routes to reduce dependence on private cars.
example2_zh: 城市可以将公共交通改善与更安全的骑行路线建设相结合，减少对私家车的依赖。
collocations: combine A with B｜把A与B结合 ; combine efforts｜合力 ; combine theory and practice｜理论与实践相结合
tip_zh: 动词重音在后；收割机名词读/ˈkɒmbaɪn/。

definition_en: an adult male, or humans in general
example1_en: A man from the bookshop helped us find the map.
example1_zh: 书店里的一位男士帮我们找到了那张地图。
example2_en: For most of history, man changed the land slowly; the last century has been different.
example2_zh: 在历史上的大部分时间里，人类改变土地的速度很慢；上一个世纪则不同。
collocations: man-made｜人造的
tip_zh: man 泛指人类时较少用于新的正式写作，更常见的是 humans 或 people。

definition_en: before the usual time | before the expected time
example1_en: I caught the early bus.
example1_zh: 我赶上了早班车。
example2_en: Early support in reading costs less than trying to repair years of failure later.
example2_zh: 早期的阅读帮助，比日后修补多年的失败更省。
collocations: early morning｜清晨 ; as early as｜早在
tip_zh: early 既可作形容词也可作副词：arrive early。

definition_en: a computer set of instructions, a show, or a plan
example1_en: The program helps students check new words.
example1_zh: 这个程序帮助学生检查生词。
example2_en: A training program for village teachers fails if it requires them to leave their classes for a month.
example2_zh: 如果乡村教师培训计划要求他们离开课堂一个月，这个计划就会失败。
collocations: computer program｜计算机程序 ; TV program｜电视节目
tip_zh: 英式拼写 programme 常指节目或计划；计算机程序英美都常用 program。

definition_en: for each
example1_en: The room costs twenty yuan per hour.
example1_zh: 这间房间每小时二十元。
example2_en: Cities that measure water use per person can see which habits waste the most.
example2_zh: 按每人用水量统计的城市，能看出哪些习惯最浪费。
collocations: per cent｜百分之 ; per person｜每人
tip_zh: per 多用于书面；口语里常用 a 或 every，如 twenty yuan an hour。

definition_en: the condition of the body or mind
example1_en: Sleep is part of health, not a reward after study.
example1_zh: 睡眠是健康的一部分，不是学完之后的奖赏。
example2_en: Poor air quality is a public health problem, not only a matter of personal choice.
example2_zh: 糟糕的空气质量是公共健康问题，不只是个人选择。
collocations: in good health｜身体健康 ; mental health｜心理健康
tip_zh: health 不可数。healthy 是形容词。

definition_en: facts about something
example1_en: The website gives information about bus times.
example1_zh: 网站提供公交时刻的信息。
example2_en: Personal information collected by a school app should not be sold to other companies.
example2_zh: 学校应用收集的个人信息，不该卖给其他公司。
collocations: a piece of information｜一条信息 ; information technology｜信息技术
tip_zh: information 不可数，不说 an information。

definition_en: to take in; to hold one's attention
example1_en: Plants absorb water through their roots.
example1_zh: 植物通过根部吸收水分。

definition_en: a social gathering, or a political group
example1_en: Our class will have a party on Friday evening.
example1_zh: 我们班周五晚上有聚会。
example2_en: A political party that never meets voters outside election season soon loses their trust.
example2_zh: 只在选举季见选民的政党，很快会失去他们的信任。
collocations: birthday party｜生日聚会 ; party member｜党员
tip_zh: party 表示聚会或党派，看语境区分。

meanings_zh: n. 外貌；出现 | n. 出现；露面
definition_en: how someone looks; the act of showing up | an occasion when someone or something becomes visible or present
example1_en: First appearance can be misleading.
example1_zh: 第一印象可能具有误导性。
example2_en: Employers should assess candidates on their skills and experience rather than judging them by their appearance.
example2_zh: 雇主应根据应聘者的技能和经验进行评估，而不是以貌取人。
collocations: physical appearance｜外貌 ; make an appearance｜露面 ; outward appearance｜外表 ; improve the appearance of｜改善……的外观
tip_zh: 外貌与露面都可用appearance；露面常用make an appearance。

definition_en: not difficult
example1_en: The first question is easy.
example1_zh: 第一题很容易。
example2_en: It is easy to blame students for being late when the bus itself never arrives on time.
example2_zh: 当公交本身从不准时，责备学生迟到是容易的。
collocations: take it easy｜别紧张 ; easy to do｜容易做
tip_zh: It is easy for sb to do。

definition_en: an object, fact, or action
example1_en: The first thing I do is open the windows.
example1_zh: 我做的第一件事是开窗。
example2_en: The hardest thing about changing a habit is not the first day but the quiet week that follows.
example2_zh: 改变一个习惯最难的不是第一天，而是之后安静的那一周。
collocations: the thing is｜问题是 ; for one thing｜首先
tip_zh: thing 很宽泛；写作里能用更具体的名词时尽量换掉。

meanings_zh: n. 基础；根据 | n. 方式；频率
definition_en: the main support or reason | The arrangement or frequency according to which something happens.
example1_en: Trust is the basis of friendship.
example1_zh: 信任是友谊的基础。
example2_en: Reliable evidence should provide the basis for government decisions about public health and environmental protection.
example2_zh: 可靠的证据应成为政府作出公共卫生和环境保护决策的依据。
collocations: on a daily basis｜每天 ; on the basis of｜根据 ; form the basis of｜构成……的基础 ; a sound basis｜坚实的基础
tip_zh: 复数为bases；on a daily basis意为每天。

meanings_zh: v. 学习；研究 | n. 学习；研究
definition_en: to spend time learning | the activity of studying
example1_en: I study English for twenty minutes a day.
example1_zh: 我每天学二十分钟英语。
example2_en: Students study better in a room that is quiet than in one filled with traffic noise.
example2_zh: 学生在安静的房间里比在充满交通噪音的房间里学得更好。
collocations: study for｜为……学习 ; study hard｜努力学习
tip_zh: study 强调系统学习；learn 强调学会。

meanings_zh: n. 费用；代价 | v. 花费
definition_en: the money or effort needed | to have a price
example1_en: The cost of the trip is fifty yuan.
example1_zh: 这次出行的费用是五十元。
example2_en: The cost of dirty air does not appear on a shop receipt, but it appears in hospital visits.
example2_zh: 脏空气的代价不会出现在购物小票上，但会出现在医院就诊里。
collocations: at the cost of｜以……为代价 ; living cost｜生活费用
tip_zh: cost 作动词的过去式仍是 cost。sth costs sb money。

definition_en: any thing at all
example1_en: Is there anything I can do to help?
example1_zh: 有什么我能帮忙的吗？
example2_en: If a report hides anything important, the public cannot judge whether a project deserves support.
example2_zh: 如果一份报告隐瞒了重要内容，公众就无法判断一个项目是否值得支持。
collocations: anything else｜其他任何事 ; anything but｜根本不
tip_zh: anything 常用于疑问句和否定句；肯定句中的“某事”用 something。

definition_en: not large
example1_en: We need a small room for the group discussion.
example1_zh: 小组讨论我们需要一间小房间。
example2_en: A small change in bus times can decide whether a student arrives before the first lesson.
example2_zh: 公交时间的一个小改动，就能决定学生是否赶得上第一节课。
collocations: small talk｜闲聊
tip_zh: small 强调尺寸不大；little 常带感情色彩。

meanings_zh: n. 事情；问题 | v. 要紧
definition_en: a subject or situation | to be important
example1_en: This is a serious matter.
example1_zh: 这是一件严肃的事。
example2_en: Housing is not a private matter when high rents push workers far from the jobs a city needs.
example2_zh: 当高房租把工人推离城市需要的工作时，住房就不是私事。
collocations: as a matter of fact｜事实上 ; no matter｜无论 ; What's the matter?｜怎么了？
tip_zh: matter 作动词是“要紧”：It matters。no matter 后接 who、what、how。

definition_en: as much or as many as needed
example1_en: There is enough paper for everyone.
example1_zh: 纸够每个人用。
example2_en: It is not enough to build a cycle lane if it ends at the busiest crossing without a light.
example2_zh: 如果自行车道在最繁忙的路口没有信号灯就中断，仅仅修建它是不够的。
collocations: enough to do｜足够做 ; more than enough｜绰绰有余
tip_zh: enough 放在形容词和副词后面：old enough；放在名词前面：enough time。

definition_en: a group of students, a lesson, or a social group
example1_en: Our class meets in Room 12.
example1_zh: 我们班在 12 室上课。
example2_en: A class of forty is hard to teach well if one teacher has no assistant.
example2_zh: 如果一位老师没有助手，四十人的班很难教好。
collocations: in class｜在课堂上 ; after class｜课后 ; class teacher｜班主任
tip_zh: class 表示课堂时 in class 不加 the。

definition_en: not many
example1_en: Few students finished the last question.
example1_zh: 很少有学生做完最后一题。
example2_en: A few trees on a hot street help, but they cannot replace a park.
example2_zh: 炎热街道上的几棵树有帮助，但替代不了一座公园。
collocations: a few｜一些 ; quite a few｜不少 ; few of｜……中很少
tip_zh: few 偏否定，几乎没有；a few 表示有一些。都用于可数名词。

definition_en: a nation, or land outside towns
example1_en: Students from five countries joined the online class.
example1_zh: 来自五个国家的学生参加了网课。
example2_en: People leave the country for the city when schools and clinics there are too far apart.
example2_zh: 当乡村的学校和诊所彼此离得太远时，人们会离开乡村去城市。
collocations: in the country｜在乡下 ; developing country｜发展中国家
tip_zh: country 表示国家时可数；the country 常指乡村。

definition_en: to know the meaning of something
example1_en: I understand the question now.
example1_zh: 我现在明白这道题了。
example2_en: Planners understand a neighbourhood better when they walk it at the hour children leave school.
example2_zh: 规划者如果在孩子放学的时刻走过一个社区，会理解得更好。
collocations: make oneself understood｜让别人听懂
tip_zh: understand 的过去式仍是 understand，不是 understanded。

definition_en: a title used before a man's surname
example1_en: Mr. Li starts the lesson at eight.
example1_zh: 李老师八点开始上课。
example2_en: A letter that begins with the wrong title, such as Mr. for a woman, can undo an otherwise polite request.
example2_zh: 一封信如果称谓用错，比如对女性用 Mr.，再礼貌的请求也会被削弱。
collocations: Mr. Smith｜史密斯先生
tip_zh: Mr. 后接姓，不接名。书写时通常作 Mr.。

meanings_zh: n. 文化 | n. 文化艺术活动 | n. 培养物
definition_en: shared customs and arts | activities involving art, music, literature and other creative work | cells or microorganisms grown under controlled conditions
example1_en: Food is part of local culture.
example1_zh: 食物是当地文化的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving local culture can strengthen community identity while allowing residents to benefit from international exchange.
example2_zh: 保护本土文化可以增强社区认同，同时让居民受益于国际交流。
collocations: local culture｜本土文化 ; cultural exchange｜文化交流 ; popular culture｜流行文化 ; bacterial culture｜细菌培养物
tip_zh: 泛指文化通常不可数；不同文化可用cultures。

meanings_zh: adj. 较年幼的；初级的 | adj. 青少年的；年少的 | n. 低年级学生；较年幼者
definition_en: younger or lower in rank | Intended for younger people or involving them | A younger person, or a student below the final year
example1_en: He is a junior member of the team.
example1_zh: 他是队里的初级成员。
example2_en: Companies should provide junior employees with structured training and regular opportunities to learn from experienced colleagues.
example2_zh: 公司应为初级员工提供系统培训，并定期安排他们向经验丰富的同事学习。
collocations: junior staff｜初级员工 ; junior position｜初级职位 ; junior championship｜青少年锦标赛
tip_zh: 职位或年龄比较用junior to，不用junior than。

definition_en: with each other
example1_en: We cleaned the classroom together.
example1_zh: 我们一起打扫了教室。
example2_en: Neighbours who cook together waste less food than families who each buy too much.
example2_zh: 一起做饭的邻居，比各自买得太多的家庭浪费的食物更少。
collocations: together with｜和……一起 ; get together｜聚会
tip_zh: together 是副词，不单独作动词。

meanings_zh: v. 帮助 | n. 帮助
definition_en: to make it easier for someone to do something | the act of helping
example1_en: Could you help me move this desk?
example1_zh: 你能帮我搬这张桌子吗？
example2_en: Older students can help younger ones settle in, which also builds leadership in the older group.
example2_zh: 高年级学生可以帮助新生适应，这也能培养他们的领导能力。
