collocations: help sb with｜在某方面帮助 ; with the help of｜在……帮助下 ; can't help doing｜忍不住
tip_zh: help sb (to) do 中的 to 可以省略。

definition_en: tall, or great in amount or level
example1_en: The shelf is too high for me to reach.
example1_zh: 架子太高，我够不着。
example2_en: High housing costs near good schools can shut out the families those schools were meant to serve.
example2_zh: 好学校附近的高房价，可能把学校本应服务的家庭挡在外面。
collocations: high school｜中学 ; at a high speed｜高速
tip_zh: 人的个子用 tall；山、价格、水平用 high。

meanings_zh: n. 平均数；一般水平 | n. 平均数；平均水平 | v. 平均为
definition_en: the usual level or mean | A value calculated by dividing a total by the item count. | Have a particular amount as the usual or calculated middle value.
example1_en: His scores are above the average.
example1_zh: 他的分数高于平均水平。
example2_en: Average household spending on energy may fall as better insulation reduces the need for heating.
example2_zh: 随着更好的隔热措施减少供暖需求，家庭能源支出的平均水平可能下降。
collocations: on average｜平均而言 ; above average｜高于平均水平 ; average income｜平均收入 ; average temperature｜平均气温
tip_zh: on average表示“平均而言”，不用in average。

definition_en: to think that something is true
example1_en: I believe we can finish the project tonight.
example1_zh: 我相信我们今晚能做完这个项目。
example2_en: Students should not believe a chart until they know who collected the numbers and why.
example2_zh: 学生在弄清数字是谁收集的、为什么收集之前，不该轻信一张图表。
collocations: believe in｜信任；信仰 ; believe it or not｜信不信由你
tip_zh: believe 后接 that 从句或 sb；believe in 表示信任或信仰。

definition_en: large in size or importance
example1_en: We need a bigger table for the group work.
example1_zh: 小组活动我们需要一张更大的桌子。
example2_en: A big sports event can fill hotels while leaving ordinary residents with higher rents.
example2_zh: 一场大型体育赛事可以住满酒店，同时让普通居民面对更高的房租。
collocations: a big deal｜一件大事
tip_zh: big 多用于口语；large 更中性，great 强调程度或情感。

definition_en: the part of the body at the end of the arm | to pass something to someone
example1_en: Please raise your hand before you speak.
example1_zh: 发言前请举手。
example2_en: A helping hand from an older student can matter more than another printed worksheet.
example2_zh: 高年级学生伸来的一只援手，可能比又一张打印的练习纸更重要。
collocations: by hand｜用手 ; on the one hand｜一方面 ; give sb a hand｜帮忙
tip_zh: hand in 是上交。hand 作动词是“递”。

meanings_zh: v. 居住；生活 | adj. 现场的；活的
definition_en: to have one's home, or to be alive | happening now, or alive
example1_en: We live near the old market.
example1_zh: 我们住在旧市场附近。
example2_en: People who live beside a busy road pay a health cost that does not appear on the rent receipt.
example2_zh: 住在繁忙道路旁的人承担着健康代价，而这不会出现在房租收据上。
collocations: live on｜以……为生 ; live up to｜不辜负
tip_zh: live 作动词读 /lɪv/；作形容词“现场的”读 /laɪv/。

meanings_zh: prep. 穿过；在对面 | adv. 横过
definition_en: from one side to the other | from one side to the other
example1_en: There is a bookshop across the street.
example1_zh: 街对面有一家书店。
example2_en: A bridge across the river can cut a student's journey from an hour to ten minutes.
example2_zh: 河上的一座桥可以把学生的路程从一小时缩短到十分钟。
collocations: come across｜偶然遇见 ; across from｜在……对面
tip_zh: across 强调从表面一边到另一边；through 强调从内部穿过。

meanings_zh: n. 邮件；岗位；柱 | v. 邮寄；张贴
definition_en: mail, a job, or a pole | to send by mail, or to put up a notice
example1_en: I will send the form by post.
example1_zh: 我会把表格寄出。
example2_en: A post in a village school is hard to fill if the teacher must travel two hours each way.
example2_zh: 如果老师每天要单程走两小时，乡村学校的岗位就很难有人来。
collocations: post office｜邮局 ; by post｜邮寄
tip_zh: post 作动词是“邮寄”或“张贴”。美式邮件多用 mail。

meanings_zh: v. 考虑；认为 | v. 认为；视为 | v. 顾及；考虑到
definition_en: to think about carefully | to have a particular opinion about someone or something | to take someone or something into account
example1_en: Please consider my advice before deciding.
example1_zh: 做决定前请考虑我的建议。
example2_en: Governments should consider the long-term environmental costs before approving major construction projects in sensitive coastal areas.
example2_zh: 政府在批准生态敏感沿海地区的大型建设项目之前，应考虑其长期环境成本。
collocations: consider doing something｜考虑做某事 ; consider the consequences｜考虑后果 ; consider all options｜考虑所有选择 ; be considered essential｜被认为必不可少
tip_zh: “考虑做”用consider doing，不用consider to do。

meanings_zh: n. 气候 | n. 社会环境；风气；氛围
definition_en: usual weather of a place | The general attitudes and conditions within a society or organisation.
example1_en: The climate here is warm and wet.
example1_zh: 这里的气候温暖潮湿。
example2_en: A changing climate may force farmers to grow different crops and adopt more efficient irrigation methods.
example2_zh: 气候变化可能迫使农民改种其他作物，并采用更高效的灌溉方法。
collocations: climate change｜气候变化 ; mild climate｜温和的气候 ; political climate｜政治环境
tip_zh: climate指长期气候，weather指具体天气。

definition_en: a location, or a position
example1_en: This is a good place to wait for the bus.
example1_zh: 这是等公交的好地方。
example2_en: Every child needs a place to study that is safe, even if that place is a shared table.
example2_zh: 每个孩子都需要一个安全的学习地方，哪怕那只是一张共用的桌子。
collocations: take place｜发生 ; in place of｜代替 ; from place to place｜到处
tip_zh: take place 表示发生，没有被动语态。

definition_en: a road vehicle with an engine
example1_en: My uncle drives a small car to work.
example1_zh: 我叔叔开一辆小汽车上班。
example2_en: Fewer car trips to school would clear the air on the narrow street outside the gate.
example2_zh: 减少开车上学的次数，能改善校门外窄街上的空气。
collocations: by car｜乘汽车 ; car park｜停车场
tip_zh: by car 不加冠词。

definition_en: a flat piece of wood, or a group that directs an organisation
example1_en: The teacher wrote the date on the board.
example1_zh: 老师把日期写在黑板上。
example2_en: A school board that never visits classrooms may not see why a class of forty is hard to teach.
example2_zh: 从不进教室的校董会，可能看不到四十人的班为什么难教。
collocations: on board｜在船/车上 ; notice board｜布告栏
tip_zh: board 作动词是“上船、上车”。

meanings_zh: v. 爱；喜爱 | n. 爱
definition_en: to feel deep affection, or to like very much | a strong feeling of affection
example1_en: I love the smell of the library in the morning.
example1_zh: 我喜欢早晨图书馆的气味。
example2_en: People who love a place are often the first to notice when its river or dialect is disappearing.
example2_zh: 热爱一个地方的人，往往最先注意到它的河流或方言正在消失。
collocations: love doing｜喜欢做 ; fall in love｜爱上
tip_zh: love 后可接 doing 或 to do，口语里 doing 更常见。

meanings_zh: v. 展示；表明 | n. 演出；展览
definition_en: to let someone see, or to prove | a public performance or display
example1_en: Show me your ticket, please.
example1_zh: 请出示你的票。
example2_en: The data show that night markets bring noise as well as income to the streets around them.
example2_zh: 数据表明，夜市给周围街道带来收入的同时，也带来噪音。
collocations: show up｜出现 ; show sb around｜带某人参观 ; on show｜在展出
tip_zh: show sb sth 双宾语；过去分词是 shown。

definition_en: to get something by paying money
example1_en: I will buy a notebook after class.
example1_zh: 课后我去买一本笔记本。
example2_en: Families buy less fresh food when the nearest market is an hour away by bus.
example2_zh: 当最近的市场要坐一小时公交时，家庭会少买新鲜食物。
collocations: buy sb sth｜给某人买 ; buy from｜从……购买
tip_zh: buy 的过去式和过去分词是 bought。

definition_en: not long, or not tall
example1_en: It is a short walk from here to the gate.
example1_zh: 从这里到门口走路不远。
example2_en: Short breaks between lessons help attention more than one long break at the end of the day.
example2_zh: 课间的短休息比一天结束时一次长休息更有助于注意力。
collocations: in short｜简言之 ; be short of｜缺少 ; short of｜缺乏
tip_zh: short 可指时间、长度或身材。shortly 是“不久”，不是“短地”。

meanings_zh: n. 报告；报道 | v. 报告；报道
definition_en: a spoken or written account | to give an account of
example1_en: Please hand in the lab report tomorrow.
example1_zh: 请明天交实验报告。
example2_en: A news report should show what is certain and what is still only a claim.
example2_zh: 新闻报道应该标明哪些是确定的，哪些仍只是说法。
collocations: weather report｜天气预报 ; report on｜关于……的报告
tip_zh: report 作动词是“报告”或“举报”：report sth to sb。

definition_en: bravery
example1_en: It takes courage to speak in public.
example1_zh: 公开演讲需要勇气。
example2_en: Young people need courage to challenge unfair practices, especially when their opinions differ from those of others.
example2_zh: 年轻人需要勇气来质疑不公平的做法，尤其是在自己的观点与他人不同时。
collocations: have the courage to do something｜有勇气做某事 ; show courage｜表现出勇气 ; take courage｜鼓起勇气
tip_zh: 通常不可数；做某事的勇气用courage to do。

meanings_zh: v. 防守；辩护 | v. 辩护；捍卫 | v. 防守
definition_en: to protect from attack | to give reasons supporting someone or something being criticised | to prevent opponents from scoring in a sport
example1_en: Soldiers defend the city from danger.
example1_zh: 士兵们保卫城市免受危险。
example2_en: Governments should defend citizens' rights while ensuring that public safety measures remain fair and proportionate.
example2_zh: 政府应捍卫公民权利，同时确保公共安全措施公平且适度。
collocations: defend against attack｜抵御攻击 ; defend human rights｜捍卫人权 ; defend a decision｜为某项决定辩护 ; defend a title｜卫冕
tip_zh: defend ... against/from ...表示保护……免受……。

meanings_zh: n. 观众；听众 | n. 读者群；受众
definition_en: people watching or listening | People who read or receive particular content
example1_en: The audience clapped after the show.
example1_zh: 演出结束后观众鼓掌。
example2_en: Online platforms enable museums to reach a wider audience, including people who cannot visit their collections in person.
example2_zh: 网络平台使博物馆能够接触更广泛的受众，包括无法亲自参观馆藏的人。
collocations: a large audience｜众多观众 ; a target audience｜目标受众 ; reach a wider audience｜触达更广泛的受众 ; audience participation｜观众参与
tip_zh: 观众多用large audience，不用many audiences。

definition_en: every person
example1_en: Everyone in our class has a reading partner.
example1_zh: 我们班每个人都有阅读伙伴。
example2_en: A park that looks open to everyone may still be hard to reach for people who use wheelchairs.
example2_zh: 一座看起来对所有人开放的公园，对使用轮椅的人仍可能很难到达。
collocations: everyone else｜其他所有人
tip_zh: everyone 作主语时谓语用单数。

definition_en: not correct
example1_en: I put the wrong date on the form.
example1_zh: 我在表格上写错了日期。
example2_en: It is wrong to judge a school only by one test if many students arrive already behind.
example2_zh: 如果许多学生入学时已经落后，只用一次考试评价学校是不对的。
collocations: go wrong｜出毛病 ; be wrong with｜……有毛病
tip_zh: wrong 作副词较少；做错事常用 do wrong 或副词 wrongly。

definition_en: something difficult that needs to be dealt with
example1_en: The main problem is the noise from the road.
example1_zh: 主要问题是路上的噪音。
example2_en: A traffic problem will not disappear if a city only widens the same road again.
example2_zh: 如果一座城市只是再次拓宽同一条路，交通问题不会消失。
collocations: no problem｜没问题 ; solve a problem｜解决问题
tip_zh: problem 是可数名词。question 是提出的问题；problem 是需要解决的困难。

definition_en: to look at and understand written words
example1_en: I read the notice twice to be sure.
example1_zh: 我把通知读了两遍以确认。
example2_en: Children who read with an adult at home often arrive at school ready to enjoy longer books.
example2_zh: 在家有成年人和他们一起阅读的孩子，上学时往往已经准备好享受更长的书。
collocations: read aloud｜朗读 ; read through｜通读
tip_zh: read 的过去式和过去分词与原形拼写相同，但读作 /red/。

definition_en: very likely
example1_en: She will probably arrive before eight.
example1_zh: 她大概会在八点前到。
example2_en: A town will probably lose young workers if the only jobs are in a city two hours away.
example2_zh: 如果仅有的工作在两小时外的城市，城镇很可能会失去年轻工人。
collocations: most probably｜最可能
tip_zh: probably 是副词；形容词是 probable。

definition_en: to work out a number
example1_en: Can you calculate the total cost?
example1_zh: 你能算出总费用吗？

meanings_zh: n. 状态；国家；州 | v. 陈述
definition_en: a condition, or a country or region | to say or write something clearly
example1_en: The classroom was in a tidy state after the meeting.
example1_zh: 会后教室很整洁。
example2_en: A state that invests in rural schools narrows the gap between villages and big cities.
example2_zh: 投资乡村学校的国家，会缩小乡村与大城市之间的差距。
collocations: in a state of｜处于……状态 ; state-owned｜国有的
tip_zh: the United States 中的 state 是州；泛指国家时也可作 state。

definition_en: one more time
example1_en: Please read the sentence again, more slowly.
example1_zh: 请再读一遍这个句子，慢一点。
example2_en: If the same street floods again, the town should stop calling it bad luck and fix the drains.
example2_zh: 如果同一条街再次积水，城镇就不该再称之为运气不好，而应修排水系统。
collocations: again and again｜一再 ; once again｜再次
tip_zh: again 不与 repeat 叠用；repeat 本身已有“再做一次”的意思。

meanings_zh: n. 灾难 | n. 彻底的失败；糟糕的事
definition_en: a sudden serious event causing harm | Something that goes extremely badly or fails completely.
example1_en: An earthquake is a natural disaster.
example1_zh: 地震是一种自然灾害。
example2_en: Effective early warning systems can reduce the damage caused by natural disasters and help communities recover more quickly.
example2_zh: 有效的预警系统可以减少自然灾害造成的损失，并帮助社区更快恢复。
collocations: natural disaster｜自然灾害 ; disaster relief｜灾害救援 ; avert disaster｜避免灾难 ; a complete disaster｜彻底的失败
tip_zh: 也可夸张形容失败：The party was a disaster。

definition_en: a standard, height, or rank
example1_en: Her reading level has improved this term.
example1_zh: 她的阅读水平这学期提高了。
example2_en: Noise levels beside a main road can be high enough to disturb an open classroom window.
example2_zh: 主干道旁的噪音水平可以高到打扰开着窗的教室。
collocations: sea level｜海平面 ; at a high level｜在高水平
tip_zh: level 作形容词是“平坦的”。

definition_en: in addition, or different
example1_en: Would anyone else like to speak?
example1_zh: 还有别人想发言吗？
example2_en: If the bus is full, students have little else to do but wait in the rain.
example2_zh: 如果公交满了，学生几乎只能在雨里等。
collocations: or else｜否则 ; something else｜别的东西
tip_zh: else 放在疑问词或不定代词后面：what else、someone else。

meanings_zh: n. 顶部；最高位置 | adj. 最高的
definition_en: the highest part or rank | highest in position or degree
example1_en: My name is at the top of the list.
example1_zh: 我的名字在名单最上面。
example2_en: Standing at the top of a test list does not show whether a student can work with other people.
example2_zh: 站在成绩榜顶端，并不能说明一个学生能否与他人合作。
collocations: on top of｜在……上面 ; top student｜优等生
tip_zh: top 作形容词表示“顶级的”：top speed。

definition_en: all of something
example1_en: I spent the whole morning in the lab.
example1_zh: 我整个上午都在实验室。
example2_en: Protecting a whole river means caring for farms and factories, not only the city section.
example2_zh: 保护整条河意味着要管农场和工厂，而不只是城区那一段。
collocations: on the whole｜总的来说 ; the whole of｜全部
tip_zh: whole 前面通常有 the 或物主代词：the whole day。

meanings_zh: n. 想法；思想 | v. 认为（think 的过去式）
definition_en: an idea or the act of thinking | past form of think
example1_en: That is a thoughtful question.
example1_zh: 那是一个有想法的问题。
example2_en: A single thoughtless comment online can follow a student longer than the mistake that caused it.
example2_zh: 网上一句欠考虑的话，可能比引发它的那个错误跟随学生更久。
collocations: at the thought of｜一想到 ; deep in thought｜陷入沉思
tip_zh: thought 也是 think 的过去式和过去分词。

meanings_zh: v. 钦佩；羡慕 | v. 欣赏；赞赏
definition_en: to respect or look up to someone | To look at something with pleasure because it is attractive
example1_en: I admire her courage in difficult times.
example1_zh: 我钦佩她在困难时期的勇气。
example2_en: People often admire successful athletes for their determination, but consistent training is equally important.
example2_zh: 人们常因成功运动员的毅力而钦佩他们，但坚持训练同样重要。
collocations: admire someone for something｜因某事钦佩某人 ; greatly admire｜十分钦佩 ; admire the view｜欣赏风景
tip_zh: admire sb for sth：因某事钦佩某人。

meanings_zh: n. 条件；状况 | n. 条件；环境 | n. 疾病；健康问题
definition_en: a state or requirement | A requirement, or circumstances affecting life or activity | A medical problem affecting someone's health
example1_en: The road is in poor condition.
example1_zh: 这条路状况很差。
example2_en: Improving working conditions can increase employee satisfaction and reduce the number of people leaving their jobs.
example2_zh: 改善工作条件可以提高员工满意度，并减少离职人数。
collocations: in good condition｜状况良好 ; working conditions｜工作条件 ; on condition that｜条件是 ; medical condition｜疾病；健康问题
tip_zh: 表状态通常不可数；表工作、生活环境常用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 转动；变成 | n. 轮流；转弯
definition_en: to move around, or to become | a chance to do something, or a change of direction
example1_en: Turn left at the bookshop.
example1_zh: 在书店处向左转。
example2_en: Parks can turn a hot street into a place where people are willing to walk.
example2_zh: 公园能把一条炎热的街道变成人们愿意步行的地方。
collocations: turn on｜打开 ; turn off｜关掉 ; turn into｜变成 ; in turn｜轮流
tip_zh: turn 加形容词表示变化：turn green。开灯用 turn on，不是 open the light。

meanings_zh: adj. 合法的；法律的 | adj. 合法的；法律允许的
definition_en: allowed by law | Allowed by the law
example1_en: Is this action legal?
example1_zh: 这个行为合法吗？
example2_en: Access to affordable legal services is essential for ensuring that disadvantaged citizens can defend their rights.
example2_zh: 让人们获得负担得起的法律服务，对保障弱势公民维护自身权利至关重要。
collocations: legal advice｜法律意见 ; legal action｜法律诉讼 ; legal rights｜法定权利 ; perfectly legal｜完全合法
tip_zh: legal可指“法律相关的”，不一定指“合法的”。

definition_en: most important
example1_en: The main entrance is on the left.
example1_zh: 正门在左边。
example2_en: The main reason for late arrivals is the bus, not a lack of interest in the first lesson.
example2_zh: 迟到的主要原因是公交，不是对第一节课缺乏兴趣。
collocations: main idea｜主旨 ; main road｜主干道
tip_zh: main 没有比较级。mainly 是副词“主要地”。

definition_en: more than two but not many
example1_en: Several students stayed to tidy the lab.
example1_zh: 几个学生留下来收拾实验室。
example2_en: Several small parks can serve a neighbourhood better than one large park that is hard to reach.
example2_zh: 几个小公园服务一个社区，可能好过一座很难到达的大公园。
collocations: several times｜几次 ; several of｜……中的几个
tip_zh: several 后接可数名词复数。

meanings_zh: prep. 直到……为止 | conj. 直到
definition_en: up to a particular time | up to the time when
example1_en: The shop is open until nine.
example1_zh: 商店营业到九点。
example2_en: A library that stays open until the last bus can serve students who cannot study at home.
example2_zh: 开到末班车的图书馆，可以服务那些无法在家学习的学生。
collocations: not...until｜直到……才 ; until now｜直到现在
tip_zh: until 可作介词或连词。not...until 表示直到……才。

definition_en: every one separately
example1_en: Each student has a different seat number.
example1_zh: 每个学生的座位号都不一样。
example2_en: Each small shop that closes on a high street takes away a place where neighbours used to talk.
example2_zh: 商业街上每关掉一家小店，就少了一个邻居们曾经聊天的地方。
collocations: each other｜互相 ; each of｜……中的每一个
tip_zh: each of 加复数名词时，谓语常用单数。

definition_en: in opposition to, or touching
example1_en: Our team will play against Class Three.
example1_zh: 我们队将和三班比赛。
example2_en: Laws against litter only work when bins are near and people see that the rules apply to everyone.
example2_zh: 禁止乱扔垃圾的法律，只有在附近有垃圾桶、而且人人都受约束时才有效。
collocations: against the law｜违法 ; be against｜反对
tip_zh: against 是介词，后面接名词、代词或 doing。

definition_en: a very short time
example1_en: Wait a moment, please.
example1_zh: 请稍等。
example2_en: The moment a rumour is shared, it is harder to replace it with a correction.
example2_zh: 谣言一经转发，就更难用更正来替换它。
collocations: at the moment｜此刻 ; in a moment｜立刻 ; the moment｜一……就
tip_zh: the moment 可引导时间从句，相当于 as soon as。

meanings_zh: n. 力量；权力；电力 | v. 驱动；供电
definition_en: strength, control, or electricity | to supply energy to a machine
example1_en: The storm cut the power for two hours.
example1_zh: 暴风雨导致停电两小时。
example2_en: The power to change a bus route should sit with people who actually ride it, not only with planners.
example2_zh: 更改公交线路的权力，应该掌握在真正乘坐它的人手里，而不只是规划者。
collocations: power station｜发电站 ; come to power｜上台 ; solar power｜太阳能
tip_zh: power 表示电力时不可数。作动词是“驱动”或“供电”。

meanings_zh: n. 专家 | adj. 专业的；熟练的
definition_en: a person with special skill | Having or showing great knowledge or skill.
example1_en: Ask an expert for advice.
example1_zh: 向专家征求建议。
example2_en: Schools should seek expert advice before introducing new technology into classrooms to support student learning.
example2_zh: 学校在将新技术引入课堂以辅助学生学习之前，应征求专家意见。
collocations: an expert on｜某方面的专家 ; expert advice｜专家建议 ; medical expert｜医学专家
tip_zh: expert on/in表示某领域的专家。

definition_en: one more, or a different one
example1_en: May I ask another question?
example1_zh: 我可以再问一个问题吗？
example2_en: Another heatwave will test whether the city's new shelters are more than a promise on paper.
example2_zh: 又一轮热浪将检验这座城市的新避暑点是否不只是纸上的承诺。
collocations: one another｜互相 ; another two｜另外两个
tip_zh: another 后接单数名词；“另外两个”可以说 another two days。

definition_en: a structure with a roof and walls
example1_en: The new building has a lift.
example1_zh: 新楼有电梯。
example2_en: An empty building in the town centre is a wasted chance to house a clinic or a library.
example2_zh: 镇中心的空楼是浪费，本可以用来做诊所或图书馆。
collocations: office building｜办公楼
tip_zh: building 是名词；build 是动词，过去式 built。

meanings_zh: adv. 最少；最不 | det. 最少的
definition_en: the smallest amount or degree | the smallest in amount
example1_en: This is the least difficult of the three questions.
example1_zh: 这是三道题里最不难的。
example2_en: The least expensive food is not always the one that keeps students awake through the afternoon.
example2_zh: 最便宜的食物不一定能让学生整个下午保持清醒。
collocations: at least｜至少 ; least of all｜最不
tip_zh: at least 表示至少；not in the least 表示一点也不。

definition_en: belonging to a whole country
example1_en: The national museum is free on Wednesdays.
example1_zh: 国家博物馆周三免费。
example2_en: A national exam should not ignore students whose schools lack labs and libraries.
example2_zh: 一场全国性考试不该忽略那些学校缺少实验室和图书馆的学生。
collocations: national flag｜国旗 ; national day｜国庆节
tip_zh: national 是形容词；国家用 nation 或 country。

definition_en: not ordinary
example1_en: Today is a special day for our school.
example1_zh: 今天对我们学校是特别的一天。
example2_en: A special bus for students works only if it arrives before the first lesson, not after.
example2_zh: 学生专车只有在第一节课前到达才有用，而不是课后。
collocations: special offer｜特价 ; nothing special｜没什么特别的
tip_zh: specially 强调专门地；especially 强调尤其。

meanings_zh: v. 向…挑战 | v. 质疑；提出异议 | v. 向…挑战；考验
definition_en: to invite someone to compete or try hard | Question whether something is true, fair, or acceptable. | Invite someone to compete or test their abilities.
example1_en: This puzzle will challenge your mind.
example1_zh: 这道谜题会挑战你的思维。
example2_en: Providing affordable housing remains a major challenge for cities experiencing rapid population growth and rising land prices.
example2_zh: 对于人口快速增长、地价不断上涨的城市而言，提供可负担住房仍是一项重大挑战。
collocations: face a challenge｜面临挑战 ; meet a challenge｜成功应对挑战 ; challenge an assumption｜质疑假设 ; challenge someone to a contest｜向某人发起比赛挑战
tip_zh: challenge作动词可直接接观点，表示质疑。

definition_en: newspapers, television, and the internet as a group
example1_en: Social media spread the news within an hour.
example1_zh: 社交媒体在一小时内传播了这条消息。
example2_en: The media can help a town prepare for a flood, or they can only arrive to film the damage.
example2_zh: 媒体可以帮助一个城镇为洪水做准备，也可以只在事后前来拍摄损失。
collocations: social media｜社交媒体 ; mass media｜大众媒体
tip_zh: media 是 medium 的复数，谓语常用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 称呼；打电话；呼唤 | n. 通话；呼唤
definition_en: to name, phone, or shout to someone | a phone conversation or a shout
example1_en: We call our teacher Mr. Chen.
example1_zh: 我们称呼老师为陈老师。
example2_en: Parents who call the school only after a problem appears miss the chance to help earlier.
example2_zh: 只在问题出现后才给学校打电话的家长，错过了更早帮忙的机会。
collocations: call on｜号召；拜访 ; call off｜取消 ; give sb a call｜给某人打电话
tip_zh: call sb sth 表示把某人称作……，中间不加 as。

meanings_zh: adj. 长的；长久的 | v. 渴望
definition_en: measuring a great length or time | to want something very much
example1_en: It was a long walk from the station.
example1_zh: 从车站走过来要很久。
example2_en: A long commute can take away the evening hours that students need for sleep and reading.
example2_zh: 漫长的通勤会占去学生需要用于睡觉和阅读的晚上时间。
collocations: before long｜不久 ; no longer｜不再 ; as long as｜只要
tip_zh: how long 询问时间或长度。long 作动词是“渴望”。

definition_en: from one side to the other, or by means of
example1_en: We walked through the market on the way home.
example1_zh: 我们回家时穿过了市场。
example2_en: Students learn more through explaining an idea than through reading the same note again.
example2_zh: 学生通过讲解一个想法学到的，往往多于把同一条笔记再读一遍。
collocations: go through｜经历；检查 ; all through｜贯穿
tip_zh: through 强调从内部穿过；across 强调从表面一边到另一边。

definition_en: the activity of using one's mind
example1_en: Critical thinking is part of the history course.
example1_zh: 批判性思考是历史课的一部分。
example2_en: Quick thinking on social media is not the same as careful thinking about a source.
example2_zh: 社交媒体上的快速思考，不等于对来源的仔细思考。
collocations: way of thinking｜思维方式
tip_zh: thinking 是 think 的 -ing，也可作名词。

meanings_zh: n. 计划 | v. 计划
definition_en: an idea for what to do | to decide what to do
example1_en: Our plan is to finish the poster today.
example1_zh: 我们的计划是今天完成海报。
example2_en: A flood plan that exists only on paper will fail the first night the river rises.
example2_zh: 只存在于纸上的防汛计划，会在河水上涨的第一个夜里失败。
collocations: plan to do｜计划做 ; make a plan｜制定计划
tip_zh: plan 作动词后接 to do，不接 doing。

meanings_zh: n. 困难 | n. 难题；困境
definition_en: a problem | A problem that makes progress or success harder.
example1_en: She overcame great difficulty to succeed.
example1_zh: 她克服巨大困难获得成功。
example2_en: Students with limited internet access may have difficulty completing assignments that require extensive online research.
example2_zh: 网络使用受限的学生可能难以完成需要大量网上研究的作业。
collocations: have difficulty doing something｜做某事有困难 ; overcome difficulties｜克服困难 ; financial difficulties｜经济困难 ; with difficulty｜费力地
tip_zh: 用have difficulty doing，不用difficulty to do。

meanings_zh: v. 支付；付出 | n. 工资
definition_en: to give money for something | money received for work
example1_en: I paid for the tickets online.
example1_zh: 我在网上付了票钱。
example2_en: Families who pay a large share of their income for rent have less left for books and clinics.
example2_zh: 把收入的很大一部分用来付房租的家庭，留给书和看病的钱就更少。
collocations: pay for｜为……付款 ; pay attention to｜注意 ; pay off｜还清；得到回报
tip_zh: pay 的过去式和过去分词是 paid。人作主语：sb pays for sth。

definition_en: having lived long, or not new
example1_en: This is an old map, but the river is the same.
example1_zh: 这是一张旧地图，但那条河还是一样的。
example2_en: Old buildings can teach a city what to keep when everything else is being rebuilt.
example2_zh: 当其他一切都在重建时，老建筑可以告诉一座城市该保留什么。
collocations: years old｜……岁 ; as old as｜和……一样老
tip_zh: 表示年龄用数字加 years old。兄姐用 elder 或 older 都可以。

definition_en: a period of seven days
example1_en: We have a test next week.
example1_zh: 我们下周有一次测验。
example2_en: A four-day school week may cut costs, but it can also lengthen each remaining day beyond what children can manage.
example2_zh: 每周上四天课也许能省钱，但也可能把剩下的每天拉长到孩子承受不了。
collocations: next week｜下周 ; once a week｜每周一次
tip_zh: next week 前不加 the。

meanings_zh: v. 包含 | v. 控制；遏制
definition_en: to have inside | to prevent something from spreading or becoming stronger
example1_en: This box may contain old letters.
example1_zh: 这个盒子里可能装有旧信。
example2_en: Processed foods often contain large amounts of salt, which can contribute to serious health problems.
example2_zh: 加工食品往往含有大量盐分，可能导致严重的健康问题。
collocations: contain ingredients｜含有成分 ; contain the spread｜遏制蔓延 ; contain costs｜控制成本 ; contain your excitement｜抑制兴奋
tip_zh: 及物动词，直接接宾语；表示“含有”时通常不用进行时。

definition_en: before noon
example1_en: The reading room opens at 7 a.m.
example1_zh: 阅览室早上七点开门。
example2_en: Starting lessons at 7 a.m. may suit adults, but many teenagers are still at their sleepiest then.
example2_zh: 早上七点上课也许适合成年人，但许多青少年那时仍处于最困的时候。
collocations: 7 a.m.｜早上七点
tip_zh: a.m. 表示午夜到中午；书写时数字与 a.m. 之间留空格。

meanings_zh: n. 过程 | v. 加工；处理
definition_en: a series of actions | to treat or deal with something in stages
example1_en: Learning a word is a slow process.
example1_zh: 学会一个词是一个缓慢的过程。
example2_en: The process of cleaning a river includes factories upstream, not only the park in the city.
example2_zh: 清理一条河的过程包括上游的工厂，而不只是城里的公园。
collocations: in the process of｜在……过程中
tip_zh: process 作动词是“加工、处理”，名词重音常在前，动词重音可在后。

definition_en: parents and children, or relatives
example1_en: My family has dinner together on Sundays.
example1_zh: 我们家周日一起吃晚饭。
example2_en: When housing is too expensive, a family may spend so much on rent that little remains for books or clinics.
example2_zh: 当住房太贵时，一个家庭可能把太多钱花在房租上，书籍和看病就所剩无几。
collocations: family name｜姓 ; family member｜家庭成员
tip_zh: family 作整体时谓语用单数；强调家庭成员时有时用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 递送；发表 | v. 发表；讲授 | v. 兑现；实现
definition_en: to take to a place; to give a speech | to give a speech, lecture, or presentation | to produce the results or benefits that were promised
example1_en: The post office will deliver the package.
example1_zh: 邮局会递送这个包裹。
example2_en: Public transport projects must deliver clear benefits to local residents if they are to justify substantial investment.
example2_zh: 公共交通项目必须为当地居民带来明确的益处，才能证明大规模投资是合理的。
collocations: deliver a parcel｜递送包裹 ; deliver a speech｜发表演讲 ; deliver results｜取得成效 ; deliver on a promise｜兑现承诺
tip_zh: 递送用deliver sth to sb；兑现承诺可用deliver on。

definition_en: to tell someone you are grateful
example1_en: I want to thank you for your help.
example1_zh: 我想谢谢你的帮助。
example2_en: Cities should thank the workers who collect rubbish before dawn, not only the people who design the posters.
example2_zh: 城市应该感谢黎明前收垃圾的工人，而不只是设计海报的人。
collocations: thank sb for｜因……感谢 ; thanks to｜多亏
tip_zh: thank 是动词，后面接人；名词用 thanks。

definition_en: a rule made by a government, or a scientific rule
example1_en: The new law limits plastic bags in shops.
example1_zh: 新法律限制商店使用塑料袋。
example2_en: A law that nobody can understand is hard to follow, even when its aim is fair.
example2_zh: 一部没人读得懂的法律很难被遵守，即使它的目的是公平的。
collocations: by law｜依法 ; break the law｜违法 ; law and order｜法治
tip_zh: law 表示法律时可不可数；一条法律用 a law。

definition_en: to be the best or to get a prize
example1_en: Our team wants to win the basketball match.
example1_zh: 我们队想赢得篮球赛。
example2_en: A city does not win public trust by announcing a plan it never carries out.
example2_zh: 一座城市不会因为宣布一个从不执行的计划就赢得公众信任。
collocations: win a prize｜获奖 ; win against｜战胜
tip_zh: win 的宾语是比赛、奖品或胜利，不是对手。打败某人用 beat sb。

definition_en: enjoyment
example1_en: The game was fun, and we also learned the words.
example1_zh: 游戏很有趣，我们还学了单词。
example2_en: Fun at a festival should not depend on so much plastic that the square is buried in waste the next day.
example2_zh: 节日的乐趣不该依赖那么多塑料，以至于第二天广场被垃圾淹没。
collocations: have fun｜玩得开心 ; for fun｜为了好玩
tip_zh: fun 是不可数名词，一般不说 a fun。funny 是“滑稽的”，不等于 fun。

definition_en: coins and notes used to buy things
example1_en: I do not have enough money for two tickets.
example1_zh: 我的钱不够买两张票。
example2_en: Money spent on early reading support can reduce the cost of failure later in secondary school.
example2_zh: 花在早期阅读辅导上的钱，可以减少中学阶段失败带来的后续成本。
collocations: pocket money｜零花钱 ; make money｜赚钱 ; save money｜省钱
tip_zh: money 不可数，不说 moneys 或 a money。

meanings_zh: n. 成就 | n. 实现；达成
definition_en: something successfully done | The successful completion of a goal through effort.
example1_en: Winning the prize was a great achievement.
example1_zh: 获奖是一项巨大成就。
example2_en: Schools should recognise creative achievements alongside examination results to encourage a wider range of student abilities.
example2_zh: 学校应在重视考试成绩的同时认可创造性成果，以鼓励学生发展多方面的能力。
collocations: a major achievement｜重大成就 ; a sense of achievement｜成就感 ; academic achievement｜学业成绩 ; the achievement of goals｜目标的实现
tip_zh: 具体成就可数；表示目标的实现时通常不可数。

definition_en: actually existing, or genuine
example1_en: Is this a real diamond or a glass one?
example1_zh: 这是真钻石还是玻璃的？
example2_en: Real progress on air quality is measured in hospital visits, not only in official announcements.
example2_zh: 空气质量的真正进步要用就诊人数来衡量，而不只是官方通报。
collocations: real life｜现实生活 ; for real｜真正地
tip_zh: real 强调实际存在；true 强调与事实相符。

definition_en: a person who is not named
example1_en: Someone left a notebook on the piano.
example1_zh: 有人把笔记本落在钢琴上了。
example2_en: Someone has to decide which bus routes stay open when a city cannot fund them all.
example2_zh: 当一座城市无法资助所有公交线路时，必须有人决定哪些线路继续开。
collocations: someone else｜其他人
tip_zh: someone 后面的形容词要后置：someone important。

meanings_zh: adv. 请 | v. 使高兴
definition_en: used to make a request polite | to make someone happy
example1_en: Please close the window before you leave.
example1_zh: 离开前请把窗户关上。
example2_en: Signs that say please are not enough if the bins are too far from where people finish their food.
example2_zh: 如果垃圾桶离人们吃完东西的地方太远，写着“请”的标牌是不够的。
collocations: yes, please｜好的，请
tip_zh: please 可放在句首或句末。pleased 表示人感到高兴。

meanings_zh: adj. 困难的；硬的；努力的 | adv. 努力地
definition_en: difficult, solid, or needing effort | with a lot of effort
example1_en: This question is hard, but not impossible.
example1_zh: 这道题难，但不是做不出。
example2_en: Hard plastic that cannot be repaired becomes waste faster than a simple tool made of wood.
example2_zh: 无法修理的硬塑料，会比一件简单的木制工具更快变成垃圾。
collocations: work hard｜努力工作 ; hard work｜艰苦的工作 ; be hard on｜对……严厉
tip_zh: hard 可以是“努力地”；hardly 是否定副词“几乎不”，二者完全不同。

meanings_zh: n. 顺序；命令；订单 | v. 命令；订购
definition_en: arrangement, a command, or a request for goods | to command, or to ask for goods
example1_en: Put the books back in the right order.
example1_zh: 把书按正确顺序放回去。
example2_en: An order to close street markets at dusk can cut noise and also cut the income of small sellers.
example2_zh: 黄昏关闭街头市场的命令能减少噪音，也会减少小贩的收入。
collocations: in order｜按顺序；状况良好 ; in order to｜为了 ; out of order｜出故障
tip_zh: in order to do 表示目的；in order that 后接句子。

definition_en: to experience a feeling or opinion
example1_en: I feel nervous before I speak in class.
example1_zh: 我在课堂上发言前感到紧张。
example2_en: Residents feel the effect of a new airport long before the official noise report is published.
example2_zh: 居民在官方噪音报告公布之前很久，就能感到新机场的影响。
collocations: feel like｜想要；感觉像 ; feel at home｜感觉自在
tip_zh: feel 作连系动词，后面接形容词：feel tired，不接 tiredly。

definition_en: an activity with rules, often for fun or sport
example1_en: Our class won the basketball game.
example1_zh: 我们班赢了篮球赛。
example2_en: A game that rewards only speed may discourage students who think carefully but slowly.
example2_zh: 只奖励速度的游戏，可能会让思考仔细但较慢的学生失去信心。
collocations: play a game｜玩游戏 ; video game｜电子游戏
tip_zh: game 可指一场比赛；match 更常用于正式体育赛事。

definition_en: only one, or not married
example1_en: A single mistake in the date can spoil the form.
example1_zh: 日期上的一个错误就能让表格作废。
example2_en: A single tree cannot cool a playground, but a row of them can.
example2_zh: 一棵树凉不了一座操场，但一排树可以。
collocations: every single｜每一个
tip_zh: single 强调仅一个；only 强调限制范围。

meanings_zh: n. 形式；表格 | v. 形成；组成
definition_en: a type or shape, or a printed document | to make or shape
example1_en: Please fill in the form in pen.
example1_zh: 请用钢笔填表。
example2_en: Friendship can take the form of sharing notes, not only of sitting together at lunch.
example2_zh: 友谊可以表现为分享笔记，而不只是午饭坐在一起。
collocations: fill in a form｜填表 ; in the form of｜以……的形式
tip_zh: form 作动词是“形成”或“组成”。

definition_en: an account of events, true or imagined
example1_en: The teacher told a short story before class ended.
example1_zh: 老师在下课前讲了一个短故事。
example2_en: A news story should name its sources, or readers cannot judge whether it is fair.
example2_zh: 一篇新闻报道应该写明来源，否则读者无法判断它是否公正。
collocations: tell a story｜讲故事 ; short story｜短篇小说
tip_zh: story 的复数是 stories。美式里 story 也可表示楼层。

meanings_zh: n. 类型 | v. 打字
definition_en: a kind or sort | to write with a keyboard
example1_en: This type of question appears every year.
example1_zh: 这类题每年都出现。
example2_en: The type of housing a city builds decides who can live near work and school.
example2_zh: 一座城市建造的住房类型，决定谁能住在工作和学校附近。
collocations: type of｜……的类型 ; a type of｜一种
tip_zh: type 作动词是“打字”。

meanings_zh: v. 确认 | v. 确认安排；正式批准
definition_en: to make sure something is true | To make an arrangement certain or give it official approval.
example1_en: Please confirm your email address.
example1_zh: 请确认你的电子邮箱地址。
example2_en: Further research is needed to confirm whether smaller classes consistently improve learning outcomes in primary schools.
example2_zh: 还需要进一步研究，以证实小学小班教学是否能持续改善学习效果。
collocations: confirm a booking｜确认预订 ; confirm that｜证实…… ; confirm a diagnosis｜确诊 ; confirm receipt｜确认收到
tip_zh: 可接名词或that从句；不要用confirm to do。

definition_en: the gas around the earth
example1_en: Open a window and let in some fresh air.
example1_zh: 开窗透透新鲜空气。
example2_en: Dirty air around a school is not a small local problem when thousands of children breathe it daily.
example2_zh: 当数千名孩子每天呼吸学校周围的脏空气时，这就不是一件小事。
collocations: by air｜乘飞机 ; fresh air｜新鲜空气 ; in the air｜在空中
tip_zh: air 通常不可数。by air 表示乘飞机。

meanings_zh: n. 申请；应用 | n. 应用；运用 | n. 应用程序
definition_en: a formal request; a use | the practical use of knowledge, skills, or methods | a computer program designed to perform particular tasks
example1_en: Send your application before Friday.
example1_zh: 周五前递交你的申请。
example2_en: Simplifying the application process could encourage more students from disadvantaged backgrounds to apply for university scholarships.
example2_zh: 简化申请流程可能鼓励更多来自弱势家庭的学生申请大学奖学金。
collocations: submit an application｜提交申请 ; application form｜申请表 ; practical application｜实际应用 ; software application｜软件应用程序
tip_zh: 申请某物用application for，向机构申请用to。

definition_en: a group working or playing together
example1_en: Our team practises on Wednesday evenings.
example1_zh: 我们队周三晚上训练。
example2_en: A rescue team is only as fast as the roads and phone signals that connect it to a village.
example2_zh: 救援队的速度，取决于连接它和村庄的道路与手机信号。
collocations: team spirit｜团队精神 ; team member｜队员
tip_zh: team 作整体时谓语可用单数；强调成员时可用复数。

definition_en: a human being
example1_en: She is the right person to ask about the map.
example1_zh: 问地图的事，她是合适的人。
example2_en: A person who cannot afford the bus may never see the museum the city is proud of.
example2_zh: 付不起公交费的人，可能永远看不到这座城市引以为傲的博物馆。
collocations: in person｜亲自 ; a person of｜一个……的人
tip_zh: person 的复数通常是 people，不常说 persons。

definition_en: a road in a town with buildings
example1_en: Our school is on a quiet street.
example1_zh: 我们学校在一条安静的街上。
example2_en: A street without a pavement pushes children into the same space as cars.
example2_zh: 没有人行道的街道，把孩子推进和汽车相同的空间。
collocations: on the street｜在街上 ; street light｜路灯
tip_zh: in the street 和 on the street 都可以，英式更常用 in。

meanings_zh: n. 头脑；心思 | v. 介意；当心
definition_en: the part of a person that thinks | to be annoyed by, or to be careful
example1_en: I changed my mind after I read the article.
example1_zh: 读完那篇文章后我改变了主意。
example2_en: A tired mind makes careless mistakes, which is why sleep belongs in any study plan.
example2_zh: 疲惫的头脑会犯粗心的错误，所以任何学习计划都该包括睡眠。
collocations: change one's mind｜改变主意 ; make up one's mind｜下定决心 ; never mind｜没关系
tip_zh: mind 作动词是“介意”：Would you mind doing...?

meanings_zh: v. 检查；核对 | n. 检查；支票（美）
definition_en: to examine to see if something is correct | an examination, or an American bank form
example1_en: Check your name before you hand in the paper.
example1_zh: 交卷前核对你的名字。
example2_en: Cities should check air quality outside schools, not only in the parks that look good in photos.
example2_zh: 城市应该检查学校外面的空气质量，而不只是照片里好看的公园。
collocations: check in｜办理入住 ; check out｜结账离开
tip_zh: check 直接接宾语。支票是 cheque（英）或 check（美）。

definition_en: coming at the end
example1_en: This is the final day to hand in the form.
example1_zh: 今天是交表的最后一天。
example2_en: A final decision on a new road should wait until residents have seen the plan.
example2_zh: 关于新路的最终决定，应该等到居民看过方案之后。
collocations: final exam｜期末考试 ; the final｜决赛
tip_zh: final 强调不可再改的最后；last 强调顺序上的最后一个。

definition_en: all things
example1_en: Everything is ready for the open day.
example1_zh: 开放日的一切都准备好了。
example2_en: A school cannot control everything a child sees online, so it should teach how to pause and check.
example2_zh: 学校无法控制孩子在网上看到的一切，所以应该教他们如何停下来核对。
collocations: everything else｜其他一切
tip_zh: everything 作主语时谓语用单数。

meanings_zh: n. 西；西方 | adj. 西方的
definition_en: the direction where the sun goes down | in or towards the west
example1_en: The sun sets in the west.
example1_zh: 太阳在西边落下。
example2_en: Towns in the west of the region share one hospital, so the road between them matters.
example2_zh: 该地区西部的城镇共用一家医院，所以它们之间的路很重要。
collocations: in the west｜在西方 ; west of｜在……以西
tip_zh: western 是形容词。the West 有时特指西方国家。

meanings_zh: n. 失败 | n. 故障；衰竭 | n. 未做；未履行
definition_en: lack of success | a situation in which a machine or organ stops working | not doing something that is expected or required
example1_en: failure can teach useful lessons.
example1_zh: 失败能教会有用的功课。
example2_en: Schools should treat failure as an opportunity for learning rather than as evidence of a student's limited ability.
example2_zh: 学校应将失败视为学习的机会，而不是学生能力有限的证明。
collocations: end in failure｜以失败告终 ; power failure｜停电 ; heart failure｜心力衰竭 ; failure to comply｜未遵守
tip_zh: 泛指失败通常不可数；a failure可指失败的事物。

meanings_zh: adj. 人的；人类的 | n. 人
definition_en: of people | a person
example1_en: Clean water is a basic human need.
example1_zh: 干净的水是人的基本需要。
example2_en: Human activity along a river, from farms to factories, decides whether the water stays drinkable.
example2_zh: 河边的人类活动，从农场到工厂，决定水是否还能饮用。
collocations: human being｜人 ; human nature｜人性
tip_zh: human 可作形容词或名词；一个人更常说 a person 或 a human being。

meanings_zh: v. 打；撞击；达到 | n. 打击；热门
definition_en: to strike, or to reach a level | a blow, or something very popular
example1_en: The ball hit the window but did not break it.
example1_zh: 球打到窗户，但没有打破。
example2_en: When summer temperatures hit a new high, schools without fans struggle to keep lessons going.
example2_zh: 当夏天气温创下新高时，没有风扇的学校很难把课继续下去。
collocations: hit sb on the head｜打某人的头
tip_zh: hit 的过去式和过去分词都是 hit。打在某人某个部位用 hit sb on the + 部位。

definition_en: the time after now
example1_en: We talked about our future plans.
example1_zh: 我们谈了未来的计划。
example2_en: The future of a riverside town depends on whether the water stays clean enough to drink.
example2_zh: 河边城镇的未来，取决于水是否仍然干净到可以饮用。
collocations: in the future｜在将来 ; in future｜从今以后
tip_zh: in the future 指将来；in future 常表示“今后”，带有从现在改起的意味。

definition_en: to move towards the speaker or a place
example1_en: Come to the hall when you hear the bell.
example1_zh: 听到铃声就到大厅来。
example2_en: New businesses come to a town only when roads, power, and schools are already reliable.
example2_zh: 只有当道路、电力和学校已经可靠时，新的商家才会来到一个城镇。
collocations: come from｜来自 ; come true｜实现 ; come up with｜想出
tip_zh: come 的过去式是 came，过去分词是 come。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……附近 | adj. 近的 | adv. 近
definition_en: close to | not far | at a short distance
example1_en: There is a bus stop near the gate.
example1_zh: 门口附近有一个公交站。
example2_en: Clinics near schools make it easier for a sick child to be seen and then return home.
example2_zh: 学校附近的诊所，让生病的孩子更容易看病然后回家。
collocations: near to｜靠近 ; nearby｜在附近
tip_zh: near 可作介词、形容词或副词。nearly 是“几乎”，不是“附近”。

definition_en: a place of higher or further education
example1_en: He hopes to study art at college.
example1_zh: 他希望在大学学艺术。
example2_en: A college far from cheap housing leaves students working nights just to pay the rent.
example2_zh: 远离廉价住房的大学，会让学生为了付房租而上夜班。
collocations: go to college｜上大学 ; college student｜大学生
tip_zh: 在美式英语里 college 常泛指大学。

meanings_zh: v. 关闭 | adj. 近的；亲密的 | adv. 接近地
definition_en: to shut | near, or intimate | near
example1_en: Please close the door quietly.
example1_zh: 请轻轻关门。
example2_en: Shops that close early leave night-shift workers with nowhere nearby to buy food.
example2_zh: 早关门的商店，让夜班工人附近没有地方买食物。
collocations: close down｜关闭 ; close to｜接近
tip_zh: close 作形容词读 /kləʊs/，表示“近的”；作动词读 /kləʊz/。

definition_en: to stay until something happens
example1_en: Please wait for me at the gate.
example1_zh: 请在门口等我。
example2_en: Children who wait for a bus in the dark need a light and a shelter, not only a timetable.
example2_zh: 在黑暗中等公交的孩子需要灯和候车亭，而不只是时刻表。
collocations: wait for｜等待 ; wait to do｜等着做 ; can't wait｜迫不及待
tip_zh: wait 是不及物动词，必须加 for 再接等待的对象。

definition_en: below, or less than
example1_en: The cat is sleeping under the desk.
example1_zh: 猫在书桌下睡觉。
example2_en: Children under six need shorter lessons and more time to move than a standard timetable allows.
example2_zh: 六岁以下的孩子需要比标准课表更短的课和更多活动时间。
collocations: under control｜处于控制中 ; under the age of｜未满……岁
tip_zh: under 可表示在下方，也可表示少于某个年龄或数量。

definition_en: able to happen or be done
example1_en: Is it possible to finish today?
example1_zh: 今天做完可能吗？
example2_en: It is possible to cut traffic if buses are frequent enough that people leave their cars at home.
example2_zh: 如果公交足够频繁、人们把车留在家里，减少车流是可能的。
collocations: as...as possible｜尽可能 ; if possible｜如果可能
tip_zh: It is possible for sb to do。possible 的主语通常是事物或 it，不是人。

definition_en: to speak words
example1_en: What did the coach say after the match?
example1_zh: 比赛后教练说了什么？
example2_en: Experts say that planting trees without caring for them later wastes both money and land.
example2_zh: 专家说，种了树却不后续养护，会同时浪费金钱和土地。
collocations: say hello｜问好 ; that is to say｜也就是说
tip_zh: say 强调说的内容；tell 后面常接人：tell sb sth。

meanings_zh: n. 过去 | prep. 经过；晚于 | adj. 过去的
definition_en: the time before now | later than, or from one side to the other | gone by in time
example1_en: The photo shows the school in the past.
example1_zh: 照片展示了过去的学校。
example2_en: A city that forgets its past may knock down the only building that tells that story.
example2_zh: 忘记过去的城市，可能会拆掉唯一讲述那段故事的建筑。
collocations: in the past｜在过去 ; past and present｜过去和现在
tip_zh: past 作介词是“经过”：walk past the gate。half past six 是六点半。

definition_en: a large amount, or a piece of land
example1_en: A lot of students take the early bus.
example1_zh: 很多学生乘早班车。
example2_en: A parking lot on a former playground shows what a school gives up when space becomes expensive.
example2_zh: 原来的操场变成停车场，说明当空间变贵时，学校放弃了什么。
collocations: a lot of｜许多 ; lots of｜许多 ; a lot｜很，非常
tip_zh: a lot of 既可接可数也可接不可数；too much 只接不可数。

meanings_zh: v. 吸引 | v. 吸引靠近
definition_en: to draw interest | Pull something closer through a physical force
example1_en: Bright colors attract many insects.
example1_zh: 鲜艳的颜色吸引许多昆虫。
example2_en: Cities that invest in reliable public transport are more likely to attract businesses and skilled workers.
example2_zh: 投资建设可靠公共交通的城市更有可能吸引企业和技术人才。
collocations: attract attention｜吸引注意 ; attract tourists｜吸引游客 ; attract investment｜吸引投资 ; attract customers｜吸引顾客
tip_zh: attract是及物动词，直接接人或事物作宾语。

meanings_zh: v. 打扰；烦恼 | v. 费心；花工夫 | n. 麻烦；烦扰
definition_en: to annoy or trouble | to make the effort to do something | trouble or effort that causes inconvenience
example1_en: Sorry to bother you so late.
example1_zh: 很抱歉这么晚打扰你。
example2_en: Constant notifications can bother students during lessons and reduce their ability to concentrate on complex tasks.
example2_zh: 持续不断的通知会在课堂上干扰学生，降低他们专注于复杂任务的能力。
collocations: bother someone with something｜拿某事打扰某人 ; bother to do something｜费心做某事 ; cannot be bothered｜懒得费事 ; a lot of bother｜很多麻烦
tip_zh: bother to do常用于否定或疑问，表示费心做。

definition_en: in spite of the fact that
example1_en: Although it was late, the library was still open.
example1_zh: 虽然晚了，图书馆还开着。
example2_en: Although a city builds more roads, traffic can grow if more people then choose to drive.
example2_zh: 尽管一座城市修建更多道路，如果更多人因此选择开车，交通仍可能增加。
collocations: although...｜虽然
tip_zh: although 引导的从句不能再加 but。可以加 yet 或 still。

definition_en: to discover something, often after looking
example1_en: I cannot find my student card.
example1_zh: 我找不到学生卡了。
example2_en: Scientists sometimes find that a cheap local method works better than an imported machine.
example2_zh: 科学家有时发现，便宜的本地方法比进口机器更有效。
collocations: find out｜查明 ; find it + adj.｜觉得……
tip_zh: find 的过去式和过去分词是 found，不是 finded。

meanings_zh: v. 跑；经营；运转 | n. 跑；一段时期
definition_en: to move quickly, manage, or operate | an act of running, or a period
example1_en: I run around the playground every morning.
example1_zh: 我每天早上绕操场跑。
example2_en: Volunteers who run a community library need a budget, not only good intentions.
example2_zh: 经营社区图书馆的志愿者需要预算，而不只是好意。
collocations: run out of｜用完 ; run after｜追赶 ; in the long run｜从长远看
tip_zh: run 的过去式是 ran，过去分词是 run。

meanings_zh: v. 不同；相异 | v. 意见不合
definition_en: to be unlike | To have a different opinion from another person.
example1_en: Opinions may differ among friends.
example1_zh: 朋友之间意见可能不同。
example2_en: Educational priorities differ between countries because economic conditions and cultural expectations shape national policies.
example2_zh: 各国的教育重点有所不同，因为经济条件和文化期待会影响国家政策。
collocations: differ from｜与……不同 ; differ in size｜大小不同 ; differ widely｜差异很大 ; differ with someone｜与某人意见不同
tip_zh: from引出比较对象，in引出差异方面。

meanings_zh: n. 光；灯 | adj. 轻的；明亮的；浅色的 | v. 点燃
definition_en: brightness, or a lamp | not heavy, or bright, or pale | to start something burning
example1_en: Please turn off the light when you leave.
example1_zh: 离开时请关灯。
example2_en: Street light makes the walk home safer, but too much light can also hide the night sky.
example2_zh: 路灯让回家的路更安全，但过多的光也会遮住夜空。
collocations: traffic light｜红绿灯 ; light up｜照亮
tip_zh: light 作形容词是“轻的”或“浅色的”，比较级 lighter。作动词“点燃”的过去式可以是 lit。

meanings_zh: adj. 一般的；总体的 | adj. 大致的；非具体的 | n. 将军
definition_en: not detailed; overall | describing main points rather than particular details | an officer with a very high rank in the army
example1_en: In general, people prefer weekends.
example1_zh: 一般来说，人们更喜欢周末。
example2_en: Although the general standard of education has improved, significant differences remain between urban and rural schools.
example2_zh: 尽管教育总体水平已有提高，城乡学校之间仍存在显著差异。
collocations: in general｜一般来说 ; general public｜公众 ; general knowledge｜常识 ; general overview｜总体概述
tip_zh: in general意为“一般来说”，常用于概括。

meanings_zh: v. 责备 | n. 责任；责备
definition_en: to say someone is responsible for a fault | Responsibility for something bad that has happened.
example1_en: Don't blame others for your mistakes.
example1_zh: 不要把自己的错误归咎于别人。
example2_en: It is unfair to blame individuals alone for environmental problems caused partly by industrial activity.
example2_zh: 环境问题部分由工业活动造成，仅归咎于个人并不公平。
collocations: blame someone for something｜因某事责怪某人 ; blame something on someone｜把某事归咎于某人 ; take the blame｜承担责任 ; be to blame｜应负责任
tip_zh: 人作宾语用blame sb for；事作宾语用blame sth on。

definition_en: to direct one's eyes, or to seem
example1_en: Look at the diagram before you answer.
example1_zh: 回答之前先看图。
example2_en: Streets that look beautiful in photos may still be unsafe if there is nowhere to cross.
example2_zh: 在照片里好看的街道，如果没有地方过马路，仍然可能不安全。
collocations: look for｜寻找 ; look after｜照顾 ; look forward to｜期待
tip_zh: look forward to 后面接名词或 doing。look 是看的动作，see 是看见。

meanings_zh: n. 公民 | n. 市民；居民
definition_en: a member of a country | A person who lives in a particular town or city.
example1_en: Every citizen has rights and duties.
example1_zh: 每个公民都有权利与义务。
example2_en: Every citizen should have access to reliable public services, regardless of income or place of residence.
example2_zh: 每位公民都应享有可靠的公共服务，不论收入多少或居住在哪里。
collocations: become a citizen｜成为公民 ; a senior citizen｜老年人 ; a responsible citizen｜负责任的公民
tip_zh: citizen强调公民身份；resident强调居住。

meanings_zh: v. 谈话；演讲 | n. 谈话；演讲
definition_en: to speak with someone | a conversation or a speech
example1_en: We talked about the class trip at lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭时我们谈了班级出游。
example2_en: Teachers who talk with students about sleep learn more than they do from a questionnaire alone.
example2_zh: 和学生谈睡眠的老师，比只看问卷了解得更多。
collocations: talk about｜谈论 ; talk to｜对……说 ; give a talk｜做演讲
tip_zh: talk 强调交谈；say 强调说出的内容。

definition_en: a room where people do written work
example1_en: The teacher is in the office now.
example1_zh: 老师现在在办公室。
example2_en: An office that stays lit all night wastes power and tells the street that nobody switched it off.
example2_zh: 整夜亮灯的办公室既费电，也向街道表明没人去关灯。
collocations: post office｜邮局 ; office building｜办公楼
tip_zh: in the office 表示在办公室里。

definition_en: a person you know and like
example1_en: My friend lent me her notes.
example1_zh: 朋友把笔记借给了我。
example2_en: A friend who checks a rumour before sharing it protects the whole class from a false story.
example2_zh: 先核对谣言再转发的朋友，能保护全班不受假消息影响。
collocations: make friends｜交朋友 ; a friend of mine｜我的一个朋友
tip_zh: make friends with sb 表示与某人交朋友。

definition_en: certain, or reliable
example1_en: Are you sure this is your bag?
example1_zh: 你确定这是你的包吗？
example2_en: Leaders should not be sure a policy works until they have asked the people who live with it.
example2_zh: 领导者在询问真正生活在政策之下的人之前，不应确信政策有效。
collocations: make sure｜确保 ; be sure to｜一定要 ; for sure｜确实
tip_zh: be sure to do 提醒某人一定要做；make sure 后面常接 that 从句。

definition_en: a set of printed pages | to arrange to have something later
example1_en: I borrowed a book from the school library.
example1_zh: 我从学校图书馆借了一本书。
example2_en: A town that closes its bookshop loses a place where people discover titles a screen did not suggest.
example2_zh: 关掉书店的城镇，失去了一个人们发现屏幕不曾推荐的书的地方。
collocations: bookshop｜书店 ; bookmark｜书签
tip_zh: book 作动词是“预订”：book a ticket。

definition_en: the place where one lives
example1_en: I left my keys at home.
example1_zh: 我把钥匙落在家里了。
example2_en: A city that offers only expensive flats cannot call itself a home for the nurses and drivers it needs.
example2_zh: 一座只提供昂贵公寓的城市，无法成为它所需的护士和司机的家。
collocations: at home｜在家 ; go home｜回家 ; feel at home｜感觉自在
tip_zh: home 前通常不加 to：go home，不是 go to home。

definition_en: the reflexive form of I
example1_en: I made the poster myself.
example1_zh: 海报是我自己做的。
example2_en: I asked myself whether a shorter shower would matter if the whole building still wasted water.
example2_zh: 我问自己，如果整栋楼仍在浪费水，缩短淋浴是否还有意义。
collocations: by myself｜独自
tip_zh: myself 作宾语或同位语，不能替代 I 作主语。

definition_en: before now, or sooner than expected
example1_en: I have already handed in the form.
example1_zh: 我已经交了表格。
example2_en: By the time a warning is issued, the river may already have risen over the path to school.
example2_zh: 等到警报发出时，河水可能已经漫过上学的小路。
collocations: already finished｜已经完成
tip_zh: already 多用于肯定句；否定和疑问里表示“尚未”常用 yet。

definition_en: a piece of music with words
example1_en: We learned a new song in music class.
example1_zh: 音乐课上我们学了一首新歌。
example2_en: A local song can keep a dialect alive when children no longer hear it at home.
example2_zh: 当孩子在家里不再听到一种方言时，一首本地歌曲能让它继续活着。
collocations: pop song｜流行歌曲 ; sing a song｜唱歌
tip_zh: song 是可数名词。

definition_en: a section of a school, shop, or government
example1_en: She works in the English department.
example1_zh: 她在英语系工作。
example2_en: A health department that shares data with schools can warn them before a heatwave arrives.
example2_zh: 与学校共享数据的卫生部门，可以在热浪到来前发出警告。
collocations: department store｜百货商店
tip_zh: department 是组织里的部门或大学的系。

meanings_zh: v. 在意；关心 | n. 小心；照料
definition_en: to feel that something is important | attention or looking after someone
example1_en: She cares about every student in the class.
example1_zh: 她关心班上的每一个学生。
example2_en: People care more about a park when they helped plant the trees than when they only walk past it.
example2_zh: 人们如果参与种过树，会比只是路过时更在意一座公园。
collocations: care about｜关心 ; care for｜照顾；喜欢 ; take care｜当心
tip_zh: care for 可以是照顾，也可以是“喜欢”，要看语境。

definition_en: an adult female person
example1_en: A woman from the clinic spoke to our class.
example1_zh: 诊所的一位女士给我们班讲了话。
example2_en: A woman who works a night shift still needs a safe way home when the last bus has gone.
example2_zh: 上夜班的妇女在末班车走后，仍然需要一条安全的回家路。
collocations: women's day｜妇女节
tip_zh: woman 的复数是 women，读音也变。

meanings_zh: adj. 下一个的；接下来的
definition_en: coming immediately after
example1_en: The next bus leaves in ten minutes.
example1_zh: 下一班车十分钟后开。
example2_en: The next step after collecting data is to ask whether the sample left anyone out.
example2_zh: 收集数据之后的下一步，是追问样本是否漏掉了什么人。
collocations: next to｜在……旁边 ; next week｜下周
tip_zh: next week 前不加 the；the next week 常指过去某个时间之后的一周。

definition_en: the organisation that keeps public order
example1_en: The police helped the children cross the road.
example1_zh: 警察帮助孩子们过马路。
example2_en: Police cannot be the only answer to a dark street; lights and pavements matter too.
example2_zh: 警察不能是黑暗街道的唯一答案；灯和人行道也很重要。
collocations: police station｜警察局 ; police officer｜警官
tip_zh: police 是集体名词，谓语常用复数。一个警察用 a police officer。

definition_en: not old
example1_en: The young trees need water every evening.
example1_zh: 这些小树每天晚上需要浇水。
example2_en: Young workers leave a town when the only jobs are far away and poorly paid.
example2_zh: 当仅有的工作又远又报酬低时，年轻工人会离开城镇。
collocations: young people｜年轻人 ; the young｜年轻人
tip_zh: the young 表示年轻人这一类，谓语用复数。

definition_en: the organ that pumps blood, or the centre
example1_en: Regular walks are good for the heart.
example1_zh: 经常走路对心脏有好处。
example2_en: A market in the heart of a town keeps daily life there; a mall on the edge can empty the centre.
example2_zh: 镇中心的市场维持着那里的日常生活；边缘的商场可能掏空中心。
collocations: heart disease｜心脏病 ; learn by heart｜记住 ; lose heart｜丧失勇气
tip_zh: by heart 表示靠记忆，不是“靠心脏”。

definition_en: before now
example1_en: The museum closed two years ago.
example1_zh: 博物馆两年前关门了。
example2_en: A factory that shut ten years ago can still leave chemicals in the soil beside a school.
example2_zh: 十年前关闭的工厂，仍可能把化学物质留在学校旁边的土壤里。
collocations: long ago｜很久以前 ; a moment ago｜刚才
tip_zh: ago 用于过去时，放在时间段后面：three days ago。不与现在完成时连用。

definition_en: a male child
example1_en: Her son walks to school with a neighbour.
example1_zh: 她儿子和邻居一起走路上学。
example2_en: A son who leaves for the city may still send money home, but the village loses his daily help.
example2_zh: 去城市的儿子也许仍会寄钱回家，但村子失去了他日常的帮忙。
collocations: son and daughter｜子女
tip_zh: son 的复数是 sons。

meanings_zh: n. 性格；角色 | n. 角色；人物 | n. 字符；文字
definition_en: personality; a person in a story | a person represented in a story, play, or film | a written or printed symbol, such as a letter
example1_en: Honesty is part of his character.
example1_zh: 诚实是他性格的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving historic buildings helps cities retain their distinctive character while adapting to modern economic demands.
example2_zh: 保护历史建筑有助于城市在适应现代经济需求的同时，保留自身的独特风貌。
collocations: main character｜主要角色 ; strength of character｜坚强品格 ; distinctive character｜独特风貌 ; Chinese characters｜汉字
tip_zh: 作“人物、字符”可数；作整体品质常不可数。

definition_en: perhaps
example1_en: Maybe we can meet after the club.
example1_zh: 也许我们可以在社团活动后见面。
example2_en: Maybe a later school start would help, but only if buses change their times too.
example2_zh: 也许推迟上学时间会有帮助，但只有公交也改时间才行。
collocations: maybe so｜也许如此
tip_zh: maybe 是一个副词；may be 是情态动词加动词，要分开写。

definition_en: to or at a distance
example1_en: She put the phone away during dinner.
example1_zh: 晚饭时她把手机收起来了。
example2_en: Moving factories away from rivers can protect drinking water for the towns downstream.
example2_zh: 把工厂迁离河流，可以保护下游城镇的饮用水。
collocations: far away｜遥远 ; right away｜立刻 ; give away｜赠送；泄露
tip_zh: away 是副词，不单独接宾语；表示离开某地用 away from。

definition_en: inside a limit of time, distance, or area
example1_en: Please reply within three days.
example1_zh: 请在三天内回复。
example2_en: A clinic within walking distance saves families the cost of a long bus ride.
example2_zh: 步行能到的诊所，能为家庭省下长途公交的费用。
collocations: within reach｜在够得着的范围内
tip_zh: within 强调不超过某个范围；in 更一般。

definition_en: a device for speaking to someone at a distance
example1_en: I left my phone in the classroom.
example1_zh: 我把电话落在教室了。
example2_en: A phone warning about a storm helps only the people who still have power and a signal.
example2_zh: 关于风暴的手机警报，只帮助那些还有电和信号的人。
collocations: on the phone｜在打电话 ; phone number｜电话号码
tip_zh: phone 作动词是“打电话”：phone sb。

meanings_zh: n. 数字；人物 | n. 人物；人影；身形 | v. 认为；估计
definition_en: a number; an important person | a person, their outline, or the shape of their body | to think or decide something after considering it
example1_en: The figure on the board is wrong.
example1_zh: 黑板上的数字错了。
example2_en: Recent employment figures suggest that investment in public transport can create substantial opportunities for local workers.
example2_zh: 近期就业数据显示，投资公共交通能为当地劳动者创造大量机会。
collocations: sales figures｜销售数据 ; a leading figure｜领军人物 ; figure out｜弄清楚 ; a rough figure｜大致数值
tip_zh: 数据常用复数figures；figure out意为弄懂。

definition_en: to succeed in doing something
example1_en: He worked hard to achieve his goals.
example1_zh: 他努力工作以实现目标。
example2_en: Governments can achieve significant reductions in air pollution by investing in clean energy and improving public transport.
example2_zh: 政府可以通过投资清洁能源和改善公共交通，大幅减少空气污染。
collocations: achieve success｜取得成功 ; achieve a goal｜实现目标 ; achieve a balance｜达到平衡 ; achieve results｜取得成果
tip_zh: 直接接目标或成果，不说achieve to do。

meanings_zh: n. 习俗；习惯 | adj. 定制的 | n. 惠顾；光顾
definition_en: a usual practice | made to meet a particular customer's needs | the business customers give to a shop or company
example1_en: Shaking hands is a common custom.
example1_zh: 握手是一种常见习俗。
example2_en: Schools can introduce children to local customs while encouraging respect for traditions from other cultures.
example2_zh: 学校可以向孩子们介绍当地风俗，同时鼓励他们尊重其他文化的传统。
collocations: local customs｜当地风俗 ; an ancient custom｜古老的习俗 ; custom furniture｜定制家具 ; regular custom｜经常光顾
tip_zh: custom指风俗或惯例；customs还可指海关。

definition_en: very nearly
example1_en: I almost missed the early bus.
example1_zh: 我差点错过早班车。
example2_en: A plan that is almost finished still fails if the last step, such as a safe crossing, is missing.
example2_zh: 一个几乎完成的计划，如果缺了最后一步，比如安全的过街处，仍然会失败。
collocations: almost all｜几乎全部 ; almost never｜几乎从不
tip_zh: almost 可修饰 all、every、no；nearly 一般不修饰 no 和 never 的否定极限，习惯上用 almost no。

definition_en: a place of higher education
example1_en: She hopes to study biology at university.
example1_zh: 她希望在大学学生物。
example2_en: A university that ignores the town around it will not see the housing problems its students face.
example2_zh: 忽视周围城镇的大学，看不到自己学生面对的住房问题。
collocations: go to university｜上大学 ; university student｜大学生
tip_zh: go to university 泛指上大学，常不加 the。

definition_en: one or the other of two
example1_en: You may take either seat.
example1_zh: 两个座位你坐哪个都行。
example2_en: Either the bus comes on time or students start arriving late, and then the first lesson suffers.
example2_zh: 要么公交准时，要么学生开始迟到，然后第一节课受影响。
collocations: either...or｜要么……要么 ; not...either｜也不
tip_zh: either...or 连接主语时，谓语与靠近的主语一致。否定句末的“也”用 either，不用 too。

definition_en: to hand something to someone, or to provide
example1_en: Please give the form to your class teacher.
example1_zh: 请把表格交给班主任。
example2_en: Cities that give buses their own lanes often move more people than cities that only widen roads.
example2_zh: 给公交车专用车道的城市，往往比只拓宽马路的城市运送更多人。
collocations: give up｜放弃 ; give out｜分发 ; give sb a hand｜帮忙
tip_zh: give sb sth 或 give sth to sb，两种语序都可以。

definition_en: used to agree or accept
example1_en: Yes, I can stay after class to help.
example1_zh: 是的，我可以课后留下来帮忙。
example2_en: A quick yes from a committee means little if nobody records who will do the work.
example2_zh: 委员会随口答应没什么用，如果没人记下谁来干活。
collocations: yes or no｜是或否
tip_zh: yes 用来肯定；对否定疑问句回答要按事实，而不是顺着问句。

meanings_zh: prep. 在……后面 | adv. 在后面
definition_en: at the back of | at the back
example1_en: The lab is behind the library.
example1_zh: 实验室在图书馆后面。
example2_en: The reasons behind a high absence rate may be buses and jobs, not only a lack of interest.
example2_zh: 高缺勤率背后的原因可能是公交和工作，而不只是缺乏兴趣。
collocations: fall behind｜落后 ; behind time｜迟到
tip_zh: behind 是介词或副词。落后用 fall behind。

meanings_zh: adj. 伟大的；极好的；巨大的
definition_en: very good, important, or large
example1_en: We had a great time at the school fair.
example1_zh: 我们在校园义卖上玩得很开心。
example2_en: A great increase in visitors can damage the very places people travel to see.
example2_zh: 游客的大量增加，可能破坏人们专程去看的那些地方。
collocations: a great deal of｜大量 ; greatly｜非常
tip_zh: a great many 后接可数名词复数。

definition_en: the reflexive form of he
example1_en: He fixed the bike himself.
example1_zh: 他自己修好了自行车。
example2_en: A mayor who walks the flooded street himself learns more than one who only reads a report.
example2_zh: 亲自走过积水街道的市长，比只读报告的市长了解得更多。
collocations: by himself｜独自
tip_zh: himself 不能代替 he 作主语。

meanings_zh: adj. 自己的 | v. 拥有
definition_en: belonging to the person mentioned | to possess
example1_en: I wrote the speech in my own words.
example1_zh: 我用自己的话写了这篇演讲。
example2_en: A town that grows its own vegetables is less shaken when outside supplies are delayed.
example2_zh: 自己种菜的城镇，在外部供应延误时受到的冲击更小。
collocations: on one's own｜独自 ; of one's own｜属于自己的
tip_zh: own 前要有物主代词：my own，不能单独说 own book。

definition_en: the two together
example1_en: Both answers are possible.
example1_zh: 两个答案都有可能。
example2_en: A city needs both affordable housing and good schools if it wants families to stay.
example2_zh: 如果一座城市希望家庭留下来，就既需要付得起的住房，也需要好学校。
collocations: both...and｜既……又 ; both of｜两者都
tip_zh: both...and... 连接并列成分，谓语用复数。

meanings_zh: adj. 慷慨的 | adj. 充足的；大量的
definition_en: willing to give | larger or more plentiful than usual or expected
example1_en: She is generous with her time.
example1_zh: 她在时间上很大方。
example2_en: Generous donations from local businesses can help community centres provide affordable activities for children and older residents.
example2_zh: 当地企业的慷慨捐助可以帮助社区中心为儿童和老年居民提供价格实惠的活动。
collocations: generous donation｜慷慨捐助 ; generous portion｜丰盛的一份 ; generous with your time｜不吝惜时间
tip_zh: be generous with sth表示在某方面慷慨。

definition_en: not different
example1_en: We took the same bus home.
example1_zh: 我们乘了同一班车回家。
example2_en: Two schools can follow the same timetable and still offer very different support to struggling students.
example2_zh: 两所学校可以执行同样的课表，但对学习吃力的学生提供的帮助仍然很不一样。
collocations: the same as｜和……一样 ; at the same time｜同时
tip_zh: same 前面通常加 the。

meanings_zh: n. 气氛；大气 | n. 大气；大气层
definition_en: the feeling of a place; air around Earth | the mixture of gases surrounding a planet
example1_en: The classroom had a friendly atmosphere.
example1_zh: 教室里气氛友好。
example2_en: A supportive classroom atmosphere encourages students to ask questions and participate more actively in discussions.
example2_zh: 相互支持的课堂氛围鼓励学生提问，并更加积极地参与讨论。
collocations: relaxed atmosphere｜轻松的氛围 ; create an atmosphere｜营造氛围 ; Earth's atmosphere｜地球大气层
tip_zh: 表示某种氛围常用an atmosphere；地球大气用the atmosphere。

definition_en: a recording of moving pictures
example1_en: We watched a short video about the river.
example1_zh: 我们看了一段关于这条河的短视频。
example2_en: A video can spread a false claim widely before anyone has time to check the pictures.
example2_zh: 一段视频可以在任何人来得及核对画面之前，把一个虚假说法传得很广。
collocations: video clip｜视频片段 ; make a video｜拍视频
tip_zh: video 可数。看视频用 watch a video。

definition_en: throughout a period of time
example1_en: Please do not talk during the exam.
example1_zh: 考试期间请不要说话。
example2_en: During a drought, schools can show families how small daily changes save a surprising amount of water.
example2_zh: 干旱期间，学校可以向家庭展示，日常的小改变能省下惊人的水量。
collocations: during the day｜在白天 ; during the holiday｜在假期期间
tip_zh: during 后接名词，不接句子；接句子用 while 或 when。

meanings_zh: adj. 谦虚的；适度的 | adj. 适度的；不大的 | adj. 穿着端庄的
definition_en: not boastful; not large | not large in size, amount, or cost | wearing clothes that do not reveal much of the body
example1_en: She is modest about her success.
example1_zh: 她对自己的成功很谦虚。
example2_en: Even a modest increase in public transport funding could improve services in rural communities.
example2_zh: 即使公共交通拨款只小幅增加，也可能改善农村社区的服务。
collocations: modest about one's achievements｜对自己的成就谦虚 ; a modest increase｜小幅增长 ; a modest income｜不高的收入
tip_zh: 形容人常指谦虚；形容数量常指不大。

meanings_zh: n. 证据 | v. 表明；证明
definition_en: facts that prove something | To show clearly that something exists or is true.
example1_en: There is no evidence of cheating.
example1_zh: 没有作弊的证据。
example2_en: Governments should consider scientific evidence before introducing policies intended to improve public health outcomes.
example2_zh: 政府在推出旨在改善公共健康状况的政策前，应考虑科学证据。
collocations: strong evidence｜有力证据 ; scientific evidence｜科学证据 ; evidence of｜……的证据 ; provide evidence｜提供证据
tip_zh: 作名词通常不可数：一项证据用a piece of evidence。

meanings_zh: n. 方法；靠近 | v. 接近；靠近 | v. 着手处理；接洽
definition_en: a way of dealing with something | To move nearer to someone or something. | To begin dealing with something or contact someone about it.
example1_en: A new approach may solve the problem.
example1_zh: 新方法可能解决这个问题。
example2_en: A balanced approach to urban planning should consider both economic growth and the protection of green spaces.
example2_zh: 均衡的城市规划方法应兼顾经济增长和绿地保护。
collocations: an approach to learning｜学习方法 ; adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; approach a problem｜着手处理问题 ; approach someone for advice｜找某人征求建议
tip_zh: 名词“方法”后用to加名词或动名词；动词后直接接宾语。

meanings_zh: adj. 道德的 | n. 寓意；教训
definition_en: about right and wrong | a lesson about right and wrong learned from a story
example1_en: The story has a moral lesson.
example1_zh: 这个故事有道德寓意。
example2_en: Companies have a moral responsibility to ensure that their suppliers provide safe working conditions.
example2_zh: 企业在道义上有责任确保其供应商提供安全的工作环境。
collocations: moral responsibility｜道德责任 ; moral dilemma｜道德困境 ; moral support｜精神支持 ; the moral of the story｜故事的寓意
tip_zh: moral指道德；morale指士气，注意拼写区别。

meanings_zh: v. 进行；指挥 | v. 传导热或电 | n. 行为；举止
definition_en: to carry out; to lead | to allow heat or electricity to pass through | the way a person behaves, especially towards others
example1_en: Scientists conduct experiments in the lab.
example1_zh: 科学家在实验室进行实验。
example2_en: Researchers should conduct thorough trials before recommending new treatments for widespread use in public hospitals.
example2_zh: 研究人员在建议公立医院广泛采用新疗法之前，应开展充分的试验。
collocations: conduct research｜开展研究 ; conduct a survey｜进行调查 ; conduct electricity｜导电 ; code of conduct｜行为准则
tip_zh: 动词重音在后；名词重音在前，英音/ˈkɒndʌkt/。

meanings_zh: v. 辩论 | v. 辩论；讨论 | v. 仔细考虑；权衡
definition_en: to discuss opposing views | To discuss a subject by considering different views. | To think carefully about options before making a decision.
example1_en: Students will debate the topic in class.
example1_zh: 学生们将在课堂上辩论这个话题。
example2_en: The debate over free public transport centres on its environmental benefits and the cost to taxpayers.
example2_zh: 关于免费公共交通的争论集中在其环境效益和纳税人需要承担的费用上。
collocations: public debate｜公开讨论 ; heated debate｜激烈的辩论 ; debate an issue｜讨论一个问题 ; debate whether to｜斟酌是否要
tip_zh: 动词可直接接议题；debate whether to表示权衡。

definition_en: helpful
example1_en: Walking is beneficial to health.
example1_zh: 散步有益健康。
example2_en: Access to green spaces is particularly beneficial to urban residents who have limited opportunities for outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 对于户外锻炼机会有限的城市居民来说，能够使用绿地尤其有益。
collocations: beneficial effect｜有益影响 ; beneficial to health｜有益健康 ; mutually beneficial｜互利的
tip_zh: 常接to或for，说明对谁或哪方面有益。

meanings_zh: n. 边界；界限 | n. 界限；限度
definition_en: a line that marks a limit | A limit defining acceptable behaviour or the scope of something
example1_en: Respect personal boundary at work.
example1_zh: 在工作中尊重个人界限。
example2_en: Clear boundaries between work and personal life can protect employees' mental health and reduce long-term stress.
example2_zh: 明确工作与个人生活的界限，可以保护员工的心理健康并减轻长期压力。
collocations: a national boundary｜国界 ; set boundaries｜设定界限 ; cross a boundary｜越过边界 ; push the boundaries｜突破界限
tip_zh: boundary 强调分界；border 常用于国家或地区边界。

meanings_zh: v. 试图；尝试 | v. 尝试；试图
definition_en: to try | To try to do something, especially something difficult.
example1_en: She will attempt to climb the mountain.
example1_zh: 她将尝试爬山。
example2_en: Many cities are attempting to reduce air pollution by improving public transport and expanding cycling networks.
example2_zh: 许多城市正通过改善公共交通和扩展自行车道网络来尝试减少空气污染。
collocations: make an attempt｜作出尝试 ; attempt to do something｜尝试做某事 ; a successful attempt｜成功的尝试 ; in an attempt to｜为了尝试
tip_zh: 动词后接to do；名词常用an attempt at doing。

meanings_zh: adj. 焦虑的；渴望的 | adj. 渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried; eager | Very eager to do something or for something to happen.
example1_en: She felt anxious before the test.
example1_zh: 考试前她感到焦虑。
example2_en: Students may become anxious about their future when career guidance is unavailable at school.
example2_zh: 学校不提供职业指导时，学生可能会对未来感到焦虑。
collocations: anxious about｜对……感到焦虑 ; anxious to please｜急于讨好 ; feel anxious｜感到焦虑
tip_zh: anxious about表担忧；anxious to do常表急切。

definition_en: to give time or energy to
example1_en: She will devote more time to study.
example1_zh: 她将把更多时间用于学习。
example2_en: Governments should devote more resources to preventive healthcare rather than relying entirely on expensive medical treatments.
example2_zh: 政府应将更多资源投入预防性医疗，而不是完全依赖昂贵的医学治疗。
collocations: devote time to｜投入时间于 ; devote resources to｜投入资源于 ; devote oneself to｜致力于
tip_zh: devote…to中的to是介词，后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 适应；改编 | v. 改编；改装
definition_en: to change to fit a new situation | to change something for a different use or audience
example1_en: Animals must adapt to climate change.
example1_zh: 动物必须适应气候变化。
example2_en: Schools must adapt their teaching methods to meet the needs of students from diverse cultural backgrounds.
example2_zh: 学校必须调整教学方法，以满足不同文化背景学生的需求。
collocations: adapt to change｜适应变化 ; adapt teaching methods｜调整教学方法 ; adapt a novel for television｜把小说改编成电视剧
tip_zh: adapt to后接名词或动名词；勿混adopt（采用）。

meanings_zh: adj. 以前的 | adj. 前者的
definition_en: previous | being the first of two people or things just mentioned
example1_en: He is a former student of this school.
example1_zh: 他是这所学校以前的学生。
example2_en: Former industrial sites can be transformed into public parks, improving urban environments and creating shared spaces.
example2_zh: 昔日的工业用地可以改建为公园，从而改善城市环境并创造共享空间。
collocations: former colleague｜以前的同事 ; former president｜前任总统 ; former industrial site｜昔日工业用地
tip_zh: the former 指两者中的前者，the latter 指后者。

definition_en: easy to see or understand
example1_en: It is evident that she studied hard.
example1_zh: 很明显她学习很努力。
example2_en: The benefits of improved public transport are evident in cities where traffic congestion has decreased.
example2_zh: 在交通拥堵有所缓解的城市，改善公共交通的益处显而易见。
collocations: clearly evident｜十分明显的 ; become evident｜变得明显 ; evident from｜从……可明显看出
tip_zh: 常用It is evident that...表示显然……。

definition_en: enough
example1_en: Food supply is adequate.
example1_zh: 食物供应是足够的。
example2_en: Schools need adequate funding to maintain safe buildings and provide effective support for students with additional needs.
example2_zh: 学校需要充足的资金来保障校舍安全，并为有额外需求的学生提供有效支持。
collocations: adequate funding｜充足的资金 ; adequate preparation｜充分准备 ; adequate for the task｜足以胜任任务
tip_zh: 表示达到所需标准，不等于优秀；常接for或to。

definition_en: real
example1_en: The actual cost was higher.
example1_zh: 实际费用更高。
example2_en: Governments should measure the actual impact of transport policies rather than relying solely on predicted benefits.
example2_zh: 政府应衡量交通政策的实际影响，而不是仅仅依赖预期收益。
collocations: actual cost｜实际成本 ; actual results｜实际结果 ; actual size｜实际大小
tip_zh: actual指实际的，不等于表示目前的current。

meanings_zh: adj. 明显的；表面上的 | adj. 表面上的；看似的
definition_en: easy to see; seeming | Seeming to be true, though possibly not actually true.
example1_en: It was apparent that he was tired.
example1_zh: 很明显他累了。
example2_en: Despite the apparent benefits of remote learning, some students struggle without direct support from teachers.
example2_zh: 尽管远程学习看似有诸多好处，一些学生在缺乏教师直接帮助时仍感到吃力。
collocations: become apparent｜变得明显 ; for no apparent reason｜无明显原因 ; apparent contradiction｜表面上的矛盾
tip_zh: 可指“明显的”，也可指“看似的”，须看语境。

meanings_zh: adj. 逐渐的 | adj. 坡度平缓的
definition_en: happening slowly | Rising or falling gently rather than steeply
example1_en: Progress is often gradual.
example1_zh: 进步往往是逐渐的。
example2_en: A gradual transition to renewable energy can help communities adapt without causing sudden job losses.
example2_zh: 逐步转向可再生能源有助于社区适应变化，避免就业岗位骤减。
collocations: gradual improvement｜逐步改善 ; gradual change｜渐进的变化 ; a gradual slope｜平缓的斜坡
tip_zh: 强调变化缓慢、分阶段；副词形式为gradually。

meanings_zh: v. 假定；承担 | v. 承担；就任 | v. 呈现；具有
definition_en: to suppose; to take on | To take on a duty, responsibility, or position. | To begin to have a particular appearance or quality.
example1_en: Don't assume that everyone knows the rules.
example1_zh: 不要假定人人都知道规则。
example2_en: Policymakers should not assume that all households have reliable internet access or adequate digital skills.
example2_zh: 政策制定者不应假定所有家庭都有稳定的网络连接或足够的数字技能。
collocations: assume that｜假定…… ; assume responsibility｜承担责任 ; assume office｜就任
tip_zh: assume常接that从句，强调未经证实便认为。

meanings_zh: v. 采用；收养 | v. 收养 | v. 正式通过；采纳
definition_en: to take up; to take as one's own | To legally take someone else's child into your family. | To formally approve a proposal, policy, or rule.
example1_en: The school will adopt a new teaching method.
example1_zh: 学校将采用一种新的教学方法。
example2_en: Governments should adopt long-term strategies that improve public transport rather than simply building more roads.
example2_zh: 政府应采取改善公共交通的长期策略，而不是一味增建道路。
collocations: adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; adopt a policy｜采纳一项政策 ; adopt a child｜收养孩子 ; adopt a resolution｜通过决议
tip_zh: adopt是采用或收养；adapt是适应或改编。

meanings_zh: n. 权威；当局 | n. 当局；主管机构 | n. 权威人士；专家
definition_en: power to make decisions | an official body responsible for a particular area or service | a person with extensive knowledge of a particular subject
example1_en: The school authority made a new rule.
example1_zh: 学校当局制定了新规则。
example2_en: Local authorities should consult residents before introducing policies that significantly affect access to public services.
example2_zh: 地方当局在推出显著影响公共服务获取的政策前，应征求居民意见。
collocations: have authority to do something｜有权做某事 ; local authorities｜地方当局 ; an authority on｜某方面的权威 ; abuse of authority｜滥用职权
tip_zh: 表权力通常不可数；the authorities常指当局。

meanings_zh: n. 贡献 | n. 捐款；捐赠物 | n. 投稿；稿件
definition_en: something given to help | Money or goods given to support a person or cause. | A piece of writing supplied for a publication.
example1_en: His contribution to science was huge.
example1_zh: 他对科学的贡献巨大。
example2_en: Public libraries make a valuable contribution to lifelong learning by providing free access to information.
example2_zh: 公共图书馆通过免费提供信息资源，为终身学习作出了宝贵贡献。
collocations: make a contribution to｜为…作出贡献 ; a significant contribution｜重大贡献 ; a voluntary contribution｜自愿捐款
tip_zh: 常用make a contribution to；to后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 欣赏；感激 | v. 欣赏；赏识 | v. 理解；意识到
definition_en: to value or be thankful for | Recognise and enjoy the value or quality of something. | Understand the importance or difficulty of a situation.
example1_en: I really appreciate your help.
example1_zh: 我真心感激你的帮助。
example2_en: Policymakers need to appreciate the difficulties rural communities face when accessing healthcare and other essential services.
example2_zh: 政策制定者需要理解农村社区在获取医疗及其他基本服务时面临的困难。
collocations: greatly appreciate｜非常感激 ; appreciate your help｜感谢你的帮助 ; appreciate the importance of｜认识到……的重要性 ; appreciate art｜欣赏艺术
tip_zh: 可接名词或动名词，不接to do；感谢帮助用appreciate your help。

meanings_zh: adj. 准确的 | adj. 精准的；命中目标的
definition_en: correct and exact | able to hit or reach the intended target
example1_en: Give an accurate answer, please.
example1_zh: 请给出准确答案。
example2_en: Accurate information about air quality enables residents to make informed decisions about outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 准确的空气质量信息能帮助居民在充分知情的情况下决定是否进行户外锻炼。
collocations: accurate information｜准确信息 ; accurate measurements｜精确测量 ; highly accurate｜高度精确的 ; an accurate prediction｜准确的预测
tip_zh: accurate强调准确无误；precise更强调细节精确。

meanings_zh: n. 自由 | n. 免受；摆脱
definition_en: the right to act freely | The state of not experiencing something unpleasant.
example1_en: Speech freedom is valued in many places.
example1_zh: 许多地方重视言论自由。
example2_en: Universities should protect academic freedom while encouraging researchers to consider the social consequences of their work.
example2_zh: 大学应保护学术自由，同时鼓励研究人员考虑其工作的社会影响。
collocations: freedom of speech｜言论自由 ; freedom to choose｜选择的自由 ; academic freedom｜学术自由 ; freedom from fear｜免于恐惧
tip_zh: freedom to do表示做某事的自由；from表示免受。

meanings_zh: adj. 基本的；根本的 | n. 基本原理；基础知识
definition_en: basic and important | A basic principle or skill, usually considered with others.
example1_en: Honesty is a fundamental value.
example1_zh: 诚实是基本价值观。
example2_en: Access to clean drinking water is a fundamental requirement for improving public health in disadvantaged communities.
example2_zh: 获得清洁饮用水是改善弱势社区公共卫生的基本条件。
collocations: fundamental to｜对……至关重要 ; a fundamental principle｜基本原则 ; fundamental change｜根本性改变 ; the fundamentals of｜……的基础知识
tip_zh: 名词通常用复数 fundamentals，表示基本原理。

meanings_zh: n. 事务；事件 | n. 婚外情；私情
definition_en: a matter or event | a romantic relationship involving someone committed to another partner
example1_en: Public affair need careful attention.
example1_zh: 公共事务需要认真关注。
example2_en: Schools can encourage young people to take an interest in current affairs through regular discussions of global events.
example2_zh: 学校可以通过定期讨论全球事件，鼓励年轻人关注时事。
collocations: current affairs｜时事 ; foreign affairs｜外交事务 ; a private affair｜私事 ; have an affair｜有婚外情
tip_zh: 表公共事务常用复数affairs，如current affairs。

meanings_zh: adj. 最初的 | n. 姓名首字母 | v. 用姓名首字母签署
definition_en: first | The first letter of a person's name | To mark a document with the first letters of your names
example1_en: My initial plan was wrong.
example1_zh: 我最初的计划是错的。
example2_en: Although the initial cost of solar panels is high, households may save money over the longer term.
example2_zh: 虽然太阳能电池板的初期费用较高，但从长远看，家庭可能节省开支。
